```{r load}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(ggrepel)
library(kableExtra)

dat <- readRDS("../../output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds") |>
  # row in the full table, which keys the precomputed replicability similarities
  mutate(perio_row = row_number()) |>
  # studies the full-text review proposes excluding: not a health vs periodontitis comparison, or a
  # systemic comorbidity in the compared groups
  filter(!grepl("^proposed exclusion", `Review status`))
excluded <- readRDS("../../output/perio_bugs_corrected.rds") |>
  filter(grepl("^proposed exclusion", `Review status`))
n_smoking_reviewed <- nrow(read.csv("../../output/llm_annotation/smoking_review.csv"))

# plotting data of the paper figures, rewritten on every render; the R scripts in figures/ draw them
fig_data_dir <- "../../output/figure_data"
dir.create(fig_data_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
export_fig_data <- \(d, name) write_csv(d, file.path(fig_data_dir, paste0(name, ".csv")), na = "")

# one row per study: metadata are shared by the increased and decreased signatures
studies <- dat |>
  distinct(Study, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(-`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, -`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, -`Abundance in Group 1`) |>
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))

# colors: health/periodontitis, periodontitis classification, profiling method
# (method colors match the overview figure of the main report; grey is always "not reported")
pal_group <- c(Health = "#2a78d6", Periodontitis = "#eb6834")

class_levels <- c(
  "Chronic periodontitis", "Chronic and aggressive periodontitis", "Aggressive periodontitis",
  "Periodontitis (stage/grade)", "Refractory periodontitis", "Periodontitis (type not specified)"
)
class_short <- c("Chronic", "Chronic + aggressive", "Aggressive", "Stage/grade", "Refractory", "Not specified")
pal_class <- setNames(c("#1baf7a", "#6250d6", "#e87ba4", "#eda100", "#e34948", "grey65"), class_short)

method_levels <- c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics", "DNA-DNA hybridization",
                   "PCR", "Other / not reported")
pal_method <- setNames(c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#008300", "#d55181", "grey65"), method_levels)

theme_meta <- theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.title = element_blank()
  )
theme_set(theme_meta)

derive_fields <- function(st) {
  mutate(st,
    classification = factor(
      class_short[match(`Periodontitis classification`, class_levels)], levels = class_short
    ),
    method = case_when(
      `Sequencing type` == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
      `Sequencing type` == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
      `Sequencing type` %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
      `Sequencing platform` == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
      .default = "Other / not reported"
    ) |> factor(levels = method_levels),
    period = cut(Year, c(-Inf, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2019, Inf),
                 labels = c("1995–2004", "2005–2009", "2010–2014", "2015–2019", "2020–2025"))
  )
}
studies <- derive_fields(studies)

# group-level measures in long format
features <- tribble(
  ~feature,   ~label,                          ~mean_col,                        ~sd_col,
  "age",      "Age (years)",                   "age mean",                       "age sd",
  "males",    "Males (%)",                     "percent males",                  NA,
  "smokers",  "Smokers (%)",                   "percent smokers",                NA,
  "pd",       "Probing depth (mm)",            "pocket depth mean (mm)",         "pocket depth sd",
  "cal",      "Clinical attachment loss (mm)", "clinical attachment loss (mm)",  "clinical attachment loss sd",
  "bop",      "Bleeding on probing (% sites)", "bleeding on probing percent",    "bleeding on probing sd",
  "plaque",   "Plaque (% sites)",              "plaque",                         "plaque sd",
  "supp",     "Suppuration (% sites)",         "suppuration percent",            "suppuration sd"
) |>
  mutate(label = factor(label, levels = label))

long <- pmap_dfr(features, function(feature, label, mean_col, sd_col) {
  map_dfr(0:1, function(g) {
    col <- function(x) if (is.na(x)) NA_real_ else studies[[paste("Group", g, x)]]
    num <- if (feature %in% c("males", "smokers")) col(paste("num", feature)) else NA_real_
    tibble(
      Study = studies$Study, feature = feature, label = label,
      group = c("Health", "Periodontitis")[g + 1],
      mean = col(mean_col), sd = col(sd_col),
      n = studies[[paste("Group", g, "sample size")]],
      num = num
    )
  })
}) |>
  # plaque indices (e.g. Silness-Löe 0-3) are not comparable with % sites
  left_join(select(studies, Study, `Plaque measure`), by = "Study") |>
  filter(!is.na(mean), feature != "plaque" | `Plaque measure` %in% "% sites") |>
  select(-`Plaque measure`)

# studies with values for both groups
paired <- long |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(Study, feature, label), names_from = group,
              values_from = c(mean, sd, n, num)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_Health), !is.na(mean_Periodontitis)) |>
  # smokers excluded from both groups: no contrast
  filter(!(feature == "smokers" & mean_Health == 0 & mean_Periodontitis == 0))

paired_tests <- paired |>
  summarise(
    studies = n(),
    diff = median(mean_Periodontitis - mean_Health),
    p = wilcox.test(mean_Periodontitis, mean_Health, paired = TRUE, exact = FALSE)$p.value,
    .by = c(feature, label)
  ) |>
  mutate(p_label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", paste("p =", signif(p, 2))))
# counts quoted in the text
paired_n <- \(f) sum(paired$feature == f)
paired_higher <- \(f) sum(paired$feature == f & paired$mean_Periodontitis > paired$mean_Health)
```

## About this report

PerioSigDB collects published signatures, lists of taxa that a study found increased or decreased in periodontitis compared with health. Each part of this report takes one question about them.

- Which studies are in PerioSigDB, how complete is their metadata, and how do they define periodontitis?
- How do the periodontitis and health groups differ in clinical measures, age and smoking, and which taxa do studies report most consistently?
- Which other conditions in BugSigDB report the same genera in the same direction, or have whole signatures like periodontitis? Colorectal cancer, head and neck cancer and smoking get a closer look.
- Do the genera that change in periodontitis also rise and fall together in the plaque of healthy people?

The metadata figures count each **study** once (n = `r nrow(studies)`). Other figures count signatures, studies or, for BugSigDB, study units; each caption says which.

**Data version:** the corrected PerioSigDB. It adds manual corrections and a full-text review of the papers to the curators' annotation, both pending curator confirmation. The review corrected or filled values such as group sizes, clinical measures, periodontitis classification and systemic health status. It also added the BugSigDB fields that PerioSigDB lacked, such as statistical test, significance threshold and multiple-testing correction. A second pass read the `r n_smoking_reviewed` studies that report smokers. It checked whether their smoking figures describe the participants behind the signature, and recorded what the signature's analysis matched on or adjusted for (`output/llm_annotation/smoking_review.csv`). `output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv` lists every change with its supporting quote.

The review proposes excluding `r n_distinct(excluded$Study)` studies (`r nrow(excluded)` signatures), and every analysis here leaves them out:

- Studies 134, 144, 155, 450, 452, 1590, 1690, 1982 and 2025-PubMed-130 are not a health vs periodontitis comparison.
- Studies 126, 766 and 2025-187 compare groups with a systemic comorbidity: dyspepsia in all participants, heart disease and diabetes in the periodontitis group, or hypertension, high cholesterol and diabetes in both groups.

Group 1 is the periodontitis group and Group 0 the comparison group. The figures label the comparison group "Health", but its eligibility criteria varied:

- Studies 298 and 153 include participants with gingivitis in Group 0.
- Studies 1752, 1818 and 1897 recruited adults aged 65 and over described as periodontitis-resistant.

::: {.callout-note}
## Terms used in this report

- **Study:** an individual published research study.
- **Signature:** a list of taxa reported as increased or decreased in one group compared with another. "Increased" and "decreased" are reported case–control differences, not changes over time.
- **Study unit:** a unique combination of study, condition, direction and body site group (BugSigDB analyses), so that a study with several similar signatures counts once.

- **Periodontitis-increased / -decreased genera:** the genera most consistently reported increased or decreased in PerioSigDB. Several health-associated oral taxa are in the decreased group, but a genus can contain species reported in both directions (e.g. *Porphyromonas gingivalis* increased, *P. catoniae* decreased).
- **FDR < 0.05:** p-values adjusted for the number of tests with the Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) method, at a false discovery rate of 5%. "Unadjusted p" is the p-value before this adjustment.
:::

The analyses use three sets of periodontitis taxa:

| Taxon set | Selection rule | Rank | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Periodontitis-associated genera (19 increased, 12 decreased) | binomial test of increased vs decreased PerioSigDB signatures, p < 0.05; includes genera that do not pass FDR | genus | targeted-panel check, direction heatmap and summary, species check, colorectal cancer stool datasets, co-occurrence |
| Consensus signatures (32 increased, 12 decreased taxa) | binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures, p < 0.05 | as reported (mostly species) | consensus taxa figure, whole-signature similarity, taxon-by-taxon heatmaps |
| Descriptive taxon sets (head and neck cancer, smoking) | reported by at least 3 studies, at least 75% in one direction; no statistical test | as reported | taxon-by-taxon heatmaps |

**Assay coverage:** about half of PerioSigDB signatures come from targeted PCR or DNA–DNA hybridization, which measure a fixed list of taxa. How often a taxon is reported therefore reflects which taxa the assays measured as well as biology. A taxon missing from a signature may have been unchanged, unreported or not measured.

# PerioSigDB overview

## Papers, signatures and taxa

```{r overview}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 8.5
#| fig-cap: "PerioSigDB overview. **(A)** Papers and signatures by publication period. **(B)** Papers per country of study population (a study from several countries counts once for each). All studies sampled subgingival plaque. Panels C–F split signatures by whether their taxa are increased or decreased in periodontitis compared with health. **(C)** Signatures listing each taxon (increased above the axis, decreased below). Labels: the 5 most frequent taxa in each direction, shown by profiling method in F. **(D)** Signature size (taxa per signature). **(E)** Profiling method of increased and decreased signatures. **(F)** Signatures containing the 5 taxa most often reported increased (top) and the 5 most often reported decreased (bottom), by direction and profiling method."
# the overview figure of the main report (paper Figure 1), on the corrected data without the proposed
# exclusions; built in its own environment so that its helpers do not replace this report's
overview <- local({
  library(sf)
  dat_condition <- dat |> mutate(comparison1 = paste(`Group 0 name`, `Group 1 name`, sep = " vs "))
  # each panel gets its own hues; grey always means "not reported"
  pal_A <- c("#1baf7a", "#4a3aa7")
  pal_CD <- c(increased = "#f1807e", decreased = "#6182a6")
  pal_EF <- c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#008300", "#d55181", "grey65")

  theme_overview <- theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm")
    )

  # panel tag at the top of the plot (so tags in a row align), x as a fraction of plot width
  tag_at <- function(x) {
    theme(
      plot.tag.location = "plot",
      plot.tag.position = c(x, 1),
      plot.tag = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, hjust = 0, vjust = 0),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 5.5, b = 5.5, l = 5.5)
    )
  }

  # Panel A: papers and signatures by publication period
  pub_period <- function(year) {
    start <- pmin(5 * (year %/% 5), 2020)
    end <- ifelse(start == 2020, max(year), start + 4)
    factor(paste0(start, "–", end), levels = rev(unique(paste0(start, "–", end)[order(start)])))
  }

  dat_period <- dat |>
    mutate(period = pub_period(as.integer(Year))) |>
    summarise(papers = n_distinct(PMID), signatures = n(), .by = period) |>
    pivot_longer(c(papers, signatures), names_to = "type", values_to = "n")

  pA <- ggplot(dat_period, aes(x = n, y = period, fill = type)) +
    geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.85), width = 0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_A) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
    labs(x = "count", y = NULL) +
    theme_overview

  # Panel B: papers per country (multi-country studies count for each country)
  country_fix <- c(
    "United States of America" = "United States",
    "South Korea" = "Republic of Korea",
    "Czechia" = "Czech Republic"
  )

  papers_per_country <- dat |>
    distinct(PMID, `Location of subjects`) |>
    separate_longer_delim(`Location of subjects`, ",") |>
    mutate(country = recode(trimws(`Location of subjects`), !!!country_fix)) |>
    distinct(PMID, country) |>
    count(country, name = "papers") |>
    mutate(papers_bin = cut(papers, breaks = c(0, 1, 4, 9, 19, Inf), labels = c("1", "2–4", "5–9", "10–19", "20+")))

  world <- spData::world |>
    filter(name_long != "Antarctica") |>
    left_join(papers_per_country, by = c("name_long" = "country"))
  stopifnot(all(papers_per_country$country %in% world$name_long))

  pB <- ggplot(world) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = papers_bin), color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("1" = "#deebf7", "2–4" = "#9ecae1", "5–9" = "#4292c6", "10–19" = "#2171b5", "20+" = "#08306b"),
      breaks = c("1", "2–4", "5–9", "10–19", "20+"), na.value = "grey85", name = "papers"
    ) +
    coord_sf(expand = FALSE) +
    theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "inside",
      legend.position.inside = c(0.01, 0.05),
      legend.justification = c(0, 0),
      legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm")
    )

  # Panels C-F are split by direction: signatures of taxa increased vs decreased in periodontitis
  msc <- bugsigdbr::getSignatures(dat_condition, tax.id.type = "metaphlan")
  sig_dir <- factor(
    ifelse(grepl("_UP$", names(msc)), "increased", "decreased"),
    levels = c("increased", "decreased")
  )
  tax_label <- function(taxon) sub("^[a-z]__", "", vapply(taxon, bugsigdbr:::.getTip, character(1)))

  # Panel C: number of signatures per taxon (increased up, decreased down), top taxa labelled
  taxon_freq_dir <- tibble(taxon = unlist(msc), direction = rep(sig_dir, lengths(msc))) |>
    count(taxon, direction, name = "signatures") |>
    mutate(label = tax_label(taxon))

  # top 5 taxa reported as increased, then top 5 reported as decreased (excluding the increased
  # five); labelled in panel C and shown by profiling method in panel F
  top_up <- taxon_freq_dir |>
    filter(direction == "increased") |>
    slice_max(signatures, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)
  top_dn <- taxon_freq_dir |>
    filter(direction == "decreased", !taxon %in% top_up$taxon) |>
    slice_max(signatures, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)
  top_taxa_dir <- bind_rows(top_up, top_dn)

  # histogram with increased signatures above the axis and decreased below, on a
  # symmetric log scale so that the many small bins remain visible
  mirror_bins <- function(value, direction, binwidth) {
    tibble(value, direction) |>
      mutate(bin = ceiling(value / binwidth)) |>
      count(direction, bin, name = "n") |>
      mutate(x = (bin - 0.5) * binwidth, y = ifelse(direction == "increased", n, -n))
  }

  mirror_hist <- function(bins, binwidth, breaks) {
    list(
      geom_col(data = bins, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = direction),
               width = binwidth, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3),
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3),
      scale_fill_manual(values = pal_CD, name = "in periodontitis"),
      scale_y_continuous(
        transform = scales::pseudo_log_trans(base = 10),
        breaks = c(-rev(breaks), breaks), labels = abs,
        expand = expansion(mult = 0.05)
      )
    )
  }

  taxon_bins <- mirror_bins(taxon_freq_dir$signatures, taxon_freq_dir$direction, binwidth = 4)

  # labels in each direction start at a common height, clear of every bar they span
  label_start <- top_taxa_dir |>
    summarise(min_x = min(signatures) - 4, .by = direction) |>
    left_join(taxon_bins, by = "direction", relationship = "one-to-many") |>
    filter(x >= min_x) |>
    summarise(label_y = 3 * max(abs(y)) * ifelse(first(direction) == "increased", 1, -1), .by = direction)

  # increased: vertical labels above the centre of each taxon's bar
  # decreased: several top taxa share a bar, so labels go in horizontal rows to the
  # right (log-spaced, nearest bar on top) with a thin line back to each bar's centre
  top_taxa_dir <- top_taxa_dir |>
    mutate(
      label = sub("^(\\w)\\w+ ", "\\1. ", label),
      bin = ceiling(signatures / 4)
    ) |>
    left_join(select(taxon_bins, direction, bin, x, y), by = c("direction", "bin")) |>
    left_join(label_start, by = "direction") |>
    arrange(direction, desc(signatures)) |>
    mutate(
      x_label = ifelse(direction == "increased", x, 30),
      label_y = ifelse(direction == "increased", label_y, -3 * 3^(row_number() - 1)),
      .by = direction
    )

  label_bars <- function(dat) {
    list(
      geom_segment(data = dat, aes(x = x, xend = x_label, y = y, yend = label_y),
                   color = "grey50", linewidth = 0.2),
      geom_text(data = filter(dat, direction == "increased"),
                aes(x = x_label, y = label_y, label = label),
                angle = 90, hjust = -0.05, size = 2.6, fontface = "italic"),
      geom_text(data = filter(dat, direction == "decreased"),
                aes(x = x_label, y = label_y, label = label),
                hjust = -0.05, size = 2.6, fontface = "italic")
    )
  }

  pD <- ggplot() +
    mirror_hist(taxon_bins, binwidth = 4, breaks = c(1, 10, 100)) +
    label_bars(top_taxa_dir) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-500, 3000)) +
    labs(x = "number of signatures", y = "number of taxa") +
    theme_overview +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  # Panel D: signature size
  pE <- ggplot() +
    mirror_hist(mirror_bins(lengths(msc), sig_dir, binwidth = 5), binwidth = 5, breaks = c(1, 10, 50)) +
    labs(x = "signature size", y = "number of signatures") +
    theme_overview +
    theme(
      legend.title = element_text(),
      legend.position = "inside",
      legend.position.inside = c(0.99, 0.02),
      legend.justification = c(1, 0),
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.background = element_blank()
    )

  # Panels E, F: profiling method of each signature
  method_levels <- c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics", "DNA-DNA hybridization",
                     "PCR", "Other / not reported")

  sig_method <- dat_condition |>
    mutate(method = case_when(
      `Sequencing type` == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
      `Sequencing type` == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
      `Sequencing type` %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
      `Sequencing platform` == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
      .default = "Other / not reported"
    )) |>
    pull(method) |>
    factor(levels = method_levels)

  method_counts <- tibble(method = sig_method, direction = sig_dir) |>
    count(direction, method) |>
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n), pct = paste0(round(100 * prop), "%"), .by = direction) |>
    mutate(direction = paste0(direction, "\n(n = ", sum(n), ")"), .by = direction) |>
    mutate(direction = fct_inorder(direction))

  pF <- ggplot(method_counts, aes(x = "", y = prop, fill = method)) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.07, pct, "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
              color = "white", size = 2.8, fontface = "bold") +
    coord_polar(theta = "y", direction = -1) +
    facet_wrap(~direction, ncol = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_EF, drop = FALSE) +
    theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

  # Panel F: the taxa labelled in panel C, by profiling method
  top_taxa <- bind_rows(top_up, top_dn)

  top_taxa_method <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(top_taxa)), function(i) {
    has_taxon <- vapply(msc, function(s) top_taxa$taxon[i] %in% s, logical(1))
    tibble(taxon = top_taxa$label[i], method = sig_method[has_taxon], direction = sig_dir[has_taxon])
  }) |>
    count(taxon, direction, method) |>
    mutate(
      n = ifelse(direction == "decreased", -n, n),
      taxon = factor(taxon, levels = rev(top_taxa$label))
    )

  pG <- ggplot(top_taxa_method, aes(x = n, y = taxon, fill = method)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.75, color = "white", linewidth = 0.3, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(top_dn) + 0.5, linewidth = 0.3, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal_EF, drop = FALSE, name = "profiling method (E, F)") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = seq(-80, 80, 20)) +
    labs(x = "number of signatures\n← decreased in periodontitis | increased in periodontitis →", y = NULL) +
    theme_overview +
    theme(
      axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
      legend.title = element_text(),
      legend.position = "inside",
      legend.position.inside = c(0.98, 0.03),
      legend.justification = c(1, 0),
      legend.direction = "vertical",
      legend.background = element_blank()
    )

  top_row <- (pA + tag_at(0.08) | pB + tag_at(0)) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1.9, 3))

  col_DE <- (pD + tag_at(0.08)) / (pE + tag_at(0.08)) + plot_layout(heights = c(1.6, 1))
  col_F <- pF + tag_at(0)
  bottom_row <- (col_DE | col_F | pG + tag_at(0.22)) + plot_layout(widths = c(1.15, 1, 1.5))

  fig <- (top_row / bottom_row) +
    plot_layout(heights = c(1, 1.3)) +
    plot_annotation(tag_levels = "A")

  # plotting data for figures/fig1.R
  export_fig_data(dat_period, "fig1_period")
  export_fig_data(papers_per_country, "fig1_country")
  world_file <- file.path(fig_data_dir, "fig1_world.geojson")
  unlink(world_file)
  sf::st_write(select(world, name_long), world_file, quiet = TRUE)
  export_fig_data(select(taxon_freq_dir, label, direction, signatures), "fig1_taxon_freq")
  export_fig_data(tibble(size = lengths(msc), direction = sig_dir, method = sig_method), "fig1_signatures")
  export_fig_data(mutate(top_taxa_method, rank = match(taxon, top_taxa$label)), "fig1_top_taxa_method")
  list(fig = fig, papers = n_distinct(dat$PMID), signatures = nrow(dat), countries = papers_per_country)
})
overview$fig
```

PerioSigDB has `r n_distinct(dat$Study)` studies and `r nrow(dat)` signatures from `r n_distinct(studies[["Location of subjects"]])` countries, led by Brazil, the United States and China. Targeted PCR and hybridization produce about half of the increased signatures, and a few classic pathogens dominate them: *P. gingivalis* and *T. forsythia* each appear in more than 60.

## Metadata completeness

```{r completeness}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 9.5
#| fig-cap: "Reporting of PerioSigDB fields across studies. Each column is a study, ordered by publication year (ticks: first study of each period). Each row is a field. Top: fields BugSigDB also records. Bottom: fields only PerioSigDB records. Group-level fields are shaded by whether both groups, one group or neither report them. Dark grey: the field does not apply to the study. Examples are the 16S variable region outside 16S sequencing, sequencing type and platform for culture and hybridization, and alpha diversity outside sequencing. LDA score applies only to LEfSe, and plaque measure only where plaque is reported. Matched on and confounders controlled for are empty when the analysis behind the signature used none. Rows that are all green, such as statistical test, source and description, come entirely from the full-text review. Green: cells that the full-text review raised (e.g. from neither or one group to both groups), not the curators. Dark and light green mean the same as dark and light blue. Percentage after each field: share of studies reporting it (for both groups, for group-level fields), among the studies it applies to."

nonempty <- \(x) !is.na(x) & !(as.character(x) %in% c("", "NA"))

# fields that only the full-text review recorded (the curators did not): reported by a study if any of its
# signatures has them, and never reported before the review
alpha_cols <- c("Pielou", "Shannon", "Chao1", "Simpson", "Inverse Simpson", "Richness")
review_reported <- dat |>
  mutate(alpha = if_any(all_of(alpha_cols), nonempty), lefse = grepl("LEfSe", `Statistical test`)) |>
  summarise(across(c(`Statistical test`, `Significance threshold`, `MHT correction`, `LDA Score above`,
                     `Data transformation`, `Matched on`, `Confounders controlled for`, Source, Description),
                   \(x) any(nonempty(x))),
            `Alpha diversity` = any(alpha), lefse = any(lefse),
            .by = Study) |>
  rename(`Multiple-testing correction` = `MHT correction`)

field_status <- function(st, review = TRUE) {
  # where a field applies (NA reported = not applicable), from the reviewed profiling method and test
  sequenced <- grepl("16S|WMS", studies$`Sequencing type`[match(st$Study, studies$Study)])
  not_sequencing <- with(studies[match(st$Study, studies$Study), ],
    is.na(`Sequencing type`) & (is.na(`Sequencing platform`) |
                                  `Sequencing platform` %in% c("DNA-DNA Hybridization", "Mass spectrometry")))
  culture <- with(studies[match(st$Study, studies$Study), ], is.na(`Sequencing type`) & is.na(`Sequencing platform`))
  plaque <- nonempty(st$`Group 0 plaque`) | nonempty(st$`Group 1 plaque`)
  only_where <- \(applies, reported) ifelse(applies, reported, NA)

  review_status <- review_reported[match(st$Study, review_reported$Study), ] |>
    mutate(across(-c(Study, lefse), \(x) x & review),
           `LDA Score above` = only_where(lefse, `LDA Score above`),
           `Alpha diversity` = only_where(sequenced, `Alpha diversity`)) |>
    select(-lefse)
  study_fields <- tibble(
    Study = st$Study,
    `Study design` = nonempty(st$`Study design`),
    `Location of subjects` = nonempty(st$`Location of subjects`),
    `Body site` = nonempty(st$`Body site`),
    `Diagnostic method` = nonempty(st$`Diagnostic method`),
    `Sequencing type` = only_where(!not_sequencing, nonempty(st$`Sequencing type`)),
    `Sequencing platform` = only_where(!culture, nonempty(st$`Sequencing platform`)),
    `16S variable region` = only_where(grepl("16S", studies$`Sequencing type`[match(st$Study, studies$Study)]),
                                       nonempty(st$`16S variable region`)),
    `Periodontitis classification` = st$classification != "Not specified",
    `Systemic health status` = nonempty(st$`Systemic condition`),
    `Group 0 definition` = nonempty(st$`Group 0 definition`),
    `Group 1 definition` = nonempty(st$`Group 1 definition`),
    `Plaque measure` = only_where(plaque, nonempty(st$`Plaque measure`))
  ) |>
    left_join(review_status, by = "Study") |>
    pivot_longer(-Study, names_to = "field", values_to = "reported") |>
    mutate(status = case_when(is.na(reported) ~ "Not applicable", reported ~ "Reported", .default = "Not reported"),
           type = "Study")

  # groups with a value, for each mean and SD
  group_cols <- features |>
    transmute(label = as.character(label), col = mean_col) |>
    add_row(label = "Sample size", col = "sample size") |>
    bind_rows(features |>
                filter(!is.na(sd_col)) |>
                transmute(label = paste(sub(" \\(.*", "", label), "SD"), col = sd_col))
  group_fields <- pmap_dfr(group_cols, function(label, col) {
    reported <- \(g) nonempty(st[[paste("Group", g, col)]])
    tibble(Study = st$Study, field = label, groups = reported(0) + reported(1))
  }) |>
    mutate(status = c("Neither group", "One group", "Both groups")[groups + 1], type = "Group")

  bind_rows(group_fields, study_fields)
}

# values before the full-text review: its changes reverted (output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv)
review_changes <- read.csv("../../output/llm_annotation/review_log.csv") |>
  filter(action == "changed", item %in% names(studies))
studies_pre <- studies
for (i in seq_len(nrow(review_changes))) {
  col <- review_changes$item[i]
  rows <- studies_pre$Study == review_changes$Study[i]
  value <- review_changes$curated[i]
  studies_pre[[col]][rows] <- if (is.numeric(studies_pre[[col]])) as.numeric(value) else value
}
studies_pre <- derive_fields(studies_pre)

status_rank <- c("Not reported" = 0, "Neither group" = 0, "One group" = 1, "Both groups" = 2, "Reported" = 1,
                 "Not applicable" = 0)

completeness <- field_status(studies) |>
  left_join(select(field_status(studies_pre, review = FALSE), Study, field, status_pre = status), by = c("Study", "field")) |>
  left_join(select(studies, Study, Year), by = "Study") |>
  mutate(
    Study = fct_reorder(Study, Year, .fun = min),
    complete = status %in% c("Both groups", "Reported"),
    filled = status_rank[status] > status_rank[status_pre]
  ) |>
  mutate(field_label = paste0(field, " (", round(100 * mean(complete[status != "Not applicable"])), "%)"),
         .by = field)

# fields BugSigDB also has (top panel) and PerioSigDB's own fields (bottom panel)
perio_only <- c("Periodontitis classification", "Systemic health status", "Plaque measure", "Diagnostic method")
completeness <- completeness |>
  mutate(set = factor(ifelse(field %in% perio_only | (type == "Group" & field != "Sample size"),
                             "PerioSigDB only", "Shared with BugSigDB"),
                      levels = c("Shared with BugSigDB", "PerioSigDB only")))

field_order <- completeness |>
  summarise(pct = mean(complete[status != "Not applicable"]), .by = field_label) |>
  arrange(pct) |>
  pull(field_label)

pal_status <- c(
  "Both groups" = "#2a78d6", "One group" = "#9ec5f4", "Neither group" = "#f0efec",
  "Reported" = "#256abf", "Not reported" = "#f0efec", "Not applicable" = "#bdb9b0",
  # cells raised by the full-text review; shade shows both groups or one group, as for blue
  "Filled by review" = "#1a9e6e", "One group (review)" = "#a3dcc3", "Reported (review)" = "#178a60"
)

# year ticks: first study of each publication period
year_ticks <- studies |>
  arrange(Year) |>
  distinct(period, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(Study, Year)

completeness <- mutate(completeness, fill = case_when(
  !filled ~ status,
  status %in% c("Both groups") ~ "Filled by review",
  .default = paste(status, "(review)")
))

ggplot(completeness, aes(x = Study, y = factor(field_label, levels = field_order), fill = fill)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_status,
                    breaks = c("Both groups", "One group", "Neither group", "Filled by review", "Not applicable")) +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = year_ticks$Study, labels = year_ticks$Year) +
  facet_grid(set ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Studies (ordered by publication year)", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank(),
        strip.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", angle = 270))
```

Reporting varies widely by field. Systemic health status and several clinical measures are often missing, and the full-text review filled many of the gaps (green).

## Periodontitis classification over time and by method

```{r classification}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "(A) Periodontitis classification of studies by publication period (share of studies; counts in bars). (B) Number of studies by classification and profiling method."

pA <- studies |>
  count(period, classification) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), .by = period) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = prop, y = fct_rev(period), fill = classification)) +
  geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop > 0.06, n, "")), position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE),
            color = "white", size = 3.2, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_class) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = "Studies", y = NULL, tag = "A") +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))

pB <- studies |>
  count(classification, method) |>
  complete(classification, method, fill = list(n = 0)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = fct_rev(classification), fill = n)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(n > 0, n, ""), color = n > 12), size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#f0efec", high = "#1c5cab", guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey15", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = "B") +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))

pA + pB + plot_layout(widths = c(1.2, 1))
```

Studies moved from the 1999 chronic/aggressive categories to the 2017 stage-and-grade system, which `r sum(studies$period == "2020–2025" & studies$classification == "Stage/grade")` of the `r sum(studies$period == "2020–2025")` studies from 2020–25 use. Stage/grade studies mostly use 16S sequencing, while chronic periodontitis was mostly studied with PCR and hybridization.

# Health vs periodontitis

## Paired study-level comparison

```{r paired-slopes}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Demographics and clinical characteristics of the periodontitis (orange) and healthy (blue) groups in each study. Small points: the group mean reported by each study, with grey lines joining the two groups of one study. Large points: median of the group means across studies, for each group separately. n: studies reporting the measure for both groups. Median difference: median across studies of each study's periodontitis minus health difference. It is not the difference between the two large points. p: paired Wilcoxon signed-rank test across studies."

medians <- long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  summarise(median = median(mean), .by = c(label, group))

strip_labels <- paired_tests |>
  arrange(label) |>
  mutate(strip = paste0(label, "\nn = ", studies, ", median difference ", sprintf("%+.2g", diff), "\n", p_label)) |>
  mutate(strip = factor(strip, levels = strip)) |>
  select(label, strip)

long |>
  semi_join(paired, by = c("Study", "feature")) |>
  left_join(strip_labels, by = "label") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group, y = mean)) +
  geom_line(aes(group = Study), color = "grey60", alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = group), size = 1, alpha = 0.6) +
  geom_line(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
            aes(y = median, group = 1), color = "grey15", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = left_join(medians, strip_labels, by = "label"),
             aes(y = median, fill = group), shape = 21, color = "white", size = 4, stroke = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~strip, scales = "free_y", nrow = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_group, guide = "none") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_group) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The clinical measures separate the groups in nearly every study: the periodontitis group has deeper pockets in all `r paired_n("pd")` studies reporting probing depth, and more attachment loss and bleeding in every study reporting them. The groups also differ in who was recruited. Periodontitis groups are older in `r paired_higher("age")` of `r paired_n("age")` studies (median +`r round(paired_tests$diff[paired_tests$feature == "age"], 1)` years) and include more smokers in `r paired_higher("smokers")` of `r paired_n("smokers")` (+`r round(paired_tests$diff[paired_tests$feature == "smokers"])` points), so age and smoking track disease status across the database.

## PerioSigDB consensus taxa

Periodontitis studies report these taxa consistently in one direction. They are shown at the rank at which they were reported (mostly species). The analyses below and the comparisons with other conditions in BugSigDB use these consensus signatures.

```{r consensus-taxa}
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-cap: "PerioSigDB consensus taxa: taxa that more PerioSigDB signatures report increased (left) or decreased (right) in periodontitis than the other way. Test: exact binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50%, unadjusted p < 0.05. Bars: signatures reporting the taxon increased (right) or decreased (left). Faded: not significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all taxa tested. Numbers: unadjusted p. Circles: participants (both groups) in the studies reporting the taxon in its consensus direction, each study counted once. Rows are ordered by p within each direction."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R
consensus_data <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")[c("consensus", "taxon_tests")]
rank_names <- c(g = "genus", f = "family", o = "order", c = "class", p = "phylum", k = "kingdom")

# terminal NCBI ID of each reported taxon, with its name and rank
sig_ids <- tibble(
  Study = dat$Study, direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  id = map(dat$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`, \(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", sub("^.*[|]", "", x))),
  full = dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`
) |>
  unnest(c(id, full))
consensus_names <- distinct(sig_ids, id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  transmute(id, rank = substr(sub("^.*[|]", "", full), 1, 1),
            name = gsub("_", " ", sub("^.*[|][a-z]__", "", full)),
            label = name)

consensus_participants <- sig_ids |>
  distinct(Study, direction, id) |>
  left_join(transmute(studies, Study, n = `Group 0 sample size` + `Group 1 sample size`), by = "Study") |>
  summarise(participants = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(id, direction))

consensus_taxa <- tibble(
  id = unlist(consensus_data$consensus),
  direction = rep(names(consensus_data$consensus), lengths(consensus_data$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(mutate(consensus_data$taxon_tests, fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")) |>
              select(id = ids, increased, decreased, p, fdr), by = "id") |>
  left_join(consensus_names, by = "id") |>
  left_join(consensus_participants, by = c("id", "direction")) |>
  arrange(p, desc(increased + decreased)) |>
  mutate(direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")),
         label = factor(label, levels = rev(unique(label))))

# shorter names in the increased panel, as in paper Figure 2A
shorten_taxon <- function(x) {
  x <- str_replace(x, "^Aggregatibacter ", "A. ")
  str_replace(x, " (bacterium|sp\\.) oral taxon", " oral taxon")
}

# one panel per direction, side by side; bars on the same scale, rows the same height
consensus_panel <- function(dir_label, title, labeller = identity) {
  d <- filter(consensus_taxa, direction == dir_label) |> mutate(label = droplevels(label))
  bars <- d |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))
  max_n <- max(abs(c(consensus_taxa$increased, consensus_taxa$decreased)))
  ggplot(bars, aes(x = n, y = label)) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = fdr < 0.05), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_text(data = d, aes(x = -max_n * 0.45, label = ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.1, color = "grey30") +
    geom_point(data = d, aes(x = max_n * 1.12, size = participants),
               shape = 21, fill = "grey65", color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = "PerioSigDB\nsignatures") +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.45),
                       labels = c(`TRUE` = "FDR < 0.05", `FALSE` = "p < 0.05"), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 4.5, limits = c(0, max(consensus_taxa$participants, na.rm = TRUE)),
                    breaks = c(500, 2000, 5000), name = "Participants") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, limits = c(-max_n * 0.62, max_n * 1.2), breaks = c(-25, 0, 25, 50, 75)) +
    scale_y_discrete(labels = labeller) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Signatures", y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic", size = 7.5),
          axis.text.x = element_text(size = 7), axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 9.5, face = "bold"))
}
n_up <- sum(consensus_taxa$direction == "Increased in periodontitis")
n_down <- sum(consensus_taxa$direction == "Decreased in periodontitis")

# the decreased panel takes the height of its rows at the top of the right column, the legends the
# space below it, so the figure spans the full width without a legend column
wrap_plots(A = consensus_panel("Increased in periodontitis", "Increased in periodontitis", labeller = shorten_taxon),
           B = consensus_panel("Decreased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis"),
           C = guide_area(), design = "AB\nAC") +
  plot_layout(heights = c(n_down, n_up - n_down), guides = "collect") &
  theme(legend.direction = "vertical", legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 7), legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
```

The increased side is led by the classic subgingival pathogens (*P. gingivalis*, *T. forsythia*, *T. denticola*), the decreased side by health-associated commensals such as *S. sanguinis*, *Corynebacterium*, *Haemophilus* and *Rothia*.

# Comparison with BugSigDB

```{r bugsigdb-load}
# BugSigDB export (cached by bugsigdbr; version date from its message or warning)
bsdb_version <- NA_character_
version_from <- function(cnd) {
  if (grepl("version from", conditionMessage(cnd))) bsdb_version <<- substr(trimws(sub(".*from ", "", conditionMessage(cnd))), 1, 10)
}
bsdb <- withCallingHandlers(
  bugsigdbr::importBugSigDB(),
  message = \(m) { version_from(m); invokeRestart("muffleMessage") },
  warning = \(w) { version_from(w); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }
)
if (is.na(bsdb_version)) bsdb_version <- format(Sys.Date())

# body site group of each listed body site: the first matching pattern wins (so skin of the cheek is skin,
# the oropharynx upper airway); sites matching none are "other" (e.g. blood, milk, pancreas)
site_rules <- c(
  skin = "^skin|^cheek$|forehead|axilla|interdigital",
  eye = "conjunctiv|tear film|eyelid|meibum|ocular",
  oral = "plaque|saliva|mouth|oral cavity|oral opening|tongue|gingiv|buccal|lip$|cheek pouch",
  `upper airway` = "pharyn|throat|nasal|nose|upper respiratory|tonsil",
  `lower airway` = "lung|sputum|bronch|trachea",
  gastrointestinal = paste0("feces|colon|colorect|intestin|caecum|cecum|rectum|rectal|ileum|ileal|jejunum|duoden|",
                            "stomach|gastric|esophag|meconium|digestive|bile"),
  urogenital = "vagin|cervi|uter|endometri|ovary|fallopian|placenta|urine|urinary|urethra|genitalia|prostate|penis"
)
site_of <- function(x) {
  x <- trimws(x)
  group <- rep("other", length(x))
  for (g in rev(names(site_rules))) group[grepl(site_rules[[g]], x, ignore.case = TRUE)] <- g
  group
}
# any of a signature's body sites is oral
is_oral <- function(sites) map_lgl(strsplit(sites, ","), \(x) any(site_of(x) == "oral"))

# BugSigDB without its periodontitis signatures (PerioSigDB is the reference for those)
bsdb_other <- filter(bsdb, !grepl("periodont", Condition, ignore.case = TRUE))

db_levels <- c("PerioSigDB", "BugSigDB")

# genera of the taxa in a signature (taxa above genus rank are dropped)
genera <- function(x) unique(sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", x[grepl("g__", x)]))

sig_genera <- function(d) {
  tibble(
    sig = seq_len(nrow(d)), Condition = d$Condition, `Body site` = d$`Body site`,
    direction = d$`Abundance in Group 1`, taxon = map(d$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, genera)
  ) |>
    unnest(taxon)
}

perio_tests <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    signatures = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
    direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased")
  )

perio_genera <- perio_tests |>
  filter(!is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(p, desc(signatures)) |>
  filter(p < 0.05) |>
  mutate(
    significance = case_when(
      fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05",
      p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05 (not FDR)",
      .default = "Not significant"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)", "Not significant"))
  )

# participants (both groups) of the PerioSigDB studies reporting each genus in its periodontitis
# direction, each study counted once
perio_participants <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  mutate(Study = dat$Study[sig]) |>
  distinct(Study, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(transmute(studies, Study, n = `Group 0 sample size` + `Group 1 sample size`), by = "Study") |>
  summarise(participants = sum(n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(taxon, direction))
perio_genera <- left_join(perio_genera, perio_participants, by = c("taxon", "direction"))

# body site group of each signature (signatures listing sites in several groups are "mixed")
site_group <- function(sites) {
  map_chr(strsplit(sites, ","), function(x) {
    groups <- unique(site_of(x))
    if (length(groups) == 1) groups else "mixed"
  })
}

# disease (or exposure) vs control comparisons only: Group 0 is a control group and Group 1 is not.
# This drops body site, time point, treatment arm, diet and reversed comparisons, which BugSigDB
# also files under the study's condition
control_names <- paste0("control|healthy|\\bhealth\\b|normal|\\bnon[- ]?|without|negative|unaffected|",
                        "\\bHC\\b|\\bNC\\b|cognitively (intact|unimpaired)|^no\\b|-free\\b|peritumo|adjacent|benign")
# BugSigDB condition labels that name the same condition (different ontology terms), merged
condition_synonyms <- c(
  "Colorectal carcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer", "Colorectal adenocarcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer",
  "Colon carcinoma" = "Colorectal cancer",
  "Major depressive disorder" = "Unipolar depression",
  "Human immunodeficiency virus" = "HIV infection",
  "Eczema" = "Atopic eczema",
  "Autism" = "Autism spectrum disorder",
  "Breast carcinoma" = "Breast cancer",
  "Esophageal carcinoma" = "Esophageal cancer",
  "Human papillomavirus" = "Human papilloma virus infection",
  "Gastric adenocarcinoma" = "Gastric cancer",
  "Prostate carcinoma" = "Prostate cancer",
  "Psoriasis vulgaris" = "Psoriasis",
  "Autoimmune type 1 diabetes" = "Type I diabetes mellitus",
  "SARS-CoV-2-related disease" = "COVID-19",
  "Constipation" = "Chronic constipation",
  # all oral, pharyngeal or laryngeal cancers
  "Squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer", "Oral squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer",
  "Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer", "Oral cavity carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer",
  "Head and neck carcinoma" = "Head and neck cancer"
)

# human disease-vs-control comparisons only (PerioSigDB is human), excluding meta-analyses, which
# re-analyse cohorts that are also in BugSigDB as primary studies
bsdb_cc <- bsdb_other |>
  filter(`Host species` == "Homo sapiens",
         !grepl("meta-analysis", `Study design`),
         grepl(control_names, `Group 0 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         !grepl(control_names, `Group 1 name`, ignore.case = TRUE),
         `Abundance in Group 1` %in% c("increased", "decreased")) |>
  mutate(Condition = coalesce(condition_synonyms[Condition], Condition))

# count each study once per condition, direction and body site group: the units below are
# study-level, and a genus is in a unit if it is in any of the study's signatures in that unit
bsdb_cc_sigs <- tibble(
  sig = seq_len(nrow(bsdb_cc)), bsdb_id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study,
  Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition, direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`,
  oral = is_oral(bsdb_cc$`Body site`),
  site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`)
) |>
  mutate(unit = as.integer(factor(paste(Study, Condition, direction, site_group, sep = "|"))))

bsdb_sigs <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  summarise(oral = any(oral), .by = c(unit, Study, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  rename(sig = unit)

bsdb_genera <- sig_genera(bsdb_cc) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_cc_sigs, sig, unit), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(sig = unit, direction, taxon)

# direction of the periodontitis genera in each condition (genera reported by >= 3 of its studies)
genus_agreement_by <- function(by = "Condition") bsdb_genera |>
  filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon) |>
  distinct(sig, taxon, direction) |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, all_of(by)), by = "sig") |>
  count(across(all_of(c(by, "taxon", "direction")))) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  left_join(select(perio_genera, taxon, perio = direction), by = "taxon") |>
  mutate(n = increased + decreased, same = ifelse(perio == "increased", increased, decreased)) |>
  filter(n >= 3)
genus_agreement <- genus_agreement_by()

# a genus agrees with periodontitis in a condition if at least two thirds of the condition's reports of it
# are in the periodontitis direction, and goes the opposite way if at most one third are; in between
# (e.g. 2 of 4) it counts as neither, i.e. against both directions
agree_cut <- 2 / 3

agreement_summary <- function(ga, by = "Condition") ga |>
  # each genus counts once
  summarise(genera = n(), agree = sum(same / n >= agree_cut), against = sum(same / n <= 1 - agree_cut),
            share = mean(same / n), .by = all_of(c(by, "perio"))) |>
  filter(genera >= 3) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = perio, values_from = c(genera, agree, against, share)) |>
  filter(!is.na(share_increased), !is.na(share_decreased)) |>
  mutate(genera = genera_increased + genera_decreased, agree = agree_increased + agree_decreased,
         # share of each genus group's genera with a clear direction (mixed genera left out) that agree
         informative_increased = agree_increased + against_increased,
         informative_decreased = agree_decreased + against_decreased,
         frac_increased = ifelse(informative_increased > 0, agree_increased / informative_increased, 0.5),
         frac_decreased = ifelse(informative_decreased > 0, agree_decreased / informative_decreased, 0.5),
         label = Condition,
         informative = informative_increased + informative_decreased,
         p = map2_dbl(agree, informative, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n)$p.value))
agreement_map <- agreement_summary(genus_agreement)
# the same within each body site group of a condition (for the body site arrows of the agreement map)
agreement_map_site <- agreement_summary(genus_agreement_by(c("Condition", "site_group")), c("Condition", "site_group"))

# left panel: PerioSigDB signatures with the genus increased (right) and decreased (left), and
# participants in the studies reporting it in its periodontitis direction (circles)
perio_panel <- function(top, genus_levels, details = TRUE, labels_right = FALSE) {
  perio_counts <- top |>
    select(taxon, increased, decreased, significance) |>
    pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
    mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n))

  max_n <- max(abs(perio_counts$n))
  p <- ggplot(perio_counts, aes(x = n, y = factor(taxon, levels = genus_levels))) +
    geom_col(aes(fill = sig_direction, alpha = significance), width = 0.7) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3)
  # without details (combined figure): no FDR values or participant circles, genus names on either side
  if (!details) {
    return(p +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                        labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"),
                        name = "PerioSigDB\nsignatures") +
      scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                         labels = c("FDR < 0.05" = "FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = "p < 0.05",
                                    "Not significant" = "Not significant"),
                         drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
      scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = pretty(c(-max_n, max_n), 3)) +
      scale_y_discrete(position = if (labels_right) "right" else "left") +
      labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
      guides(fill = "none", alpha = "none") +
      theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic")))
  }
  p +
    geom_text(data = distinct(top, taxon, fdr),
              aes(x = -max_n * 1.05, label = ifelse(fdr < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", fdr))),
              hjust = 1, size = 2.5, color = "grey30") +
    geom_point(data = distinct(top, taxon, participants), aes(x = max_n * 1.35, size = participants),
               shape = 21, fill = "grey65", color = "grey20", stroke = 0.3) +
    scale_size_area(max_size = 6.5, limits = c(0, max(perio_genera$participants)), breaks = c(500, 2000, 5000),
                    name = "Participants") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6"),
                      labels = c(increased = "Increased", decreased = "Decreased"), name = NULL) +
    scale_alpha_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = 1, "p < 0.05 (not FDR)" = 0.6, "Not significant" = 0.25),
                       drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, breaks = scales::breaks_extended()(c(-max_n, max_n)),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.35, 0.25))) +
    labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures\n(left: FDR; circles: participants)", y = NULL) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1, ncol = 1), alpha = guide_legend(order = 2, ncol = 1),
           size = guide_legend(order = 3, ncol = 1)) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical", legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
          legend.key.size = unit(0.35, "cm"))
}

# top bar: share of each column's signatures from oral body sites
oral_panel <- function(columns, axis_right = FALSE) {
  p <- ggplot(columns, aes(x = col, y = oral)) +
    geom_col(fill = "grey60", width = 0.7) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 1), limits = c(0, 1),
                       position = if (axis_right) "right" else "left") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Oral sites") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank())
  # columns split into blocks (direction heatmaps): one panel per block, as in the heatmap
  if ("block" %in% names(columns)) {
    p <- p + facet_grid(. ~ block, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
      theme(strip.text = element_blank(), strip.background = element_blank(),
            panel.spacing.x = unit(0.3, "cm"))
  }
  p
}

# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it increased vs decreased against 50% (the same test as for PerioSigDB),
# BH-adjusted across all genus x condition tests
# direction of each genus within each BugSigDB condition: exact binomial test of signatures
# reporting it in the same vs the opposite direction as periodontitis
count_directions <- function(d, ...) {
  d |>
    count(..., taxon, direction) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                  decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))()
}
direction_test <- function(d, dir) {
  d |>
    mutate(
      n = increased + decreased,
      same = if (dir == "increased") increased else decreased,
      share_same = same / n,
      p = map2_dbl(same, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
      fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH")
    )
}
# body site subsets, candidates for the direction heatmap alongside the whole conditions: a condition's
# study units from one body site group (units spanning several groups are not a subset). They face the same
# thresholds as conditions.
site_subsets <- bsdb_sigs |>
  distinct(Condition, site_group) |>
  filter(site_group != "mixed") |>
  transmute(Condition, site_group,
            subset = paste0(Condition, " (", coalesce(c(oral = "mouth", gastrointestinal = "gut",
                                                        "upper airway" = "airway", "lower airway" = "lung")[site_group],
                                                      site_group), ")"))
# BugSigDB study units, with the units of each body site subset added again under the subset's name
sigs_with_subsets <- function() {
  bind_rows(bsdb_sigs,
            inner_join(bsdb_sigs, site_subsets, by = c("Condition", "site_group")) |>
              mutate(Condition = subset) |> select(-subset))
}
direction_hits <- function(dir, subsets = FALSE) {
  bsdb_genera |>
    filter(taxon %in% perio_genera$taxon[perio_genera$direction == dir]) |>
    distinct(sig, taxon) |>
    left_join(select(if (subsets) sigs_with_subsets() else bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, direction), by = "sig",
              relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    filter(direction %in% c("increased", "decreased"))
}
direction_tests <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5) {
  sizes <- sigs_with_subsets() |> count(Condition, name = "signatures") |> filter(signatures >= min_sigs)
  tests <- direction_hits(dir, subsets = TRUE) |>
    filter(Condition %in% sizes$Condition) |>
    count_directions(Condition) |>
    direction_test(dir)
  # FDR of the conditions as before (body site subsets not part of their family); the subsets'
  # FDR adjusted together with all conditions
  is_subset <- tests$Condition %in% site_subsets$subset
  tests$fdr[!is_subset] <- p.adjust(tests$p[!is_subset], method = "BH")
  tests
}

# per condition and genus group: genera reported by at least min_reports of the condition's studies
# (agreement counts), how many agree with periodontitis (at least agree_cut of their reports in the
# periodontitis direction) and how many go the opposite way (at most 1 - agree_cut); genera in between
# (mixed) have no clear direction and are left out, as in a sign test; informative = agree + against
direction_agreement <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3) {
  direction_tests(dir, min_sigs) |>
    filter(n >= min_reports) |>
    summarise(genera = n(), agree = sum(same / n >= agree_cut), against = sum(same / n <= 1 - agree_cut),
              .by = Condition) |>
    mutate(informative = agree + against, mixed = genera - informative) |>
    filter(informative > 0) |>
    mutate(p = map2_dbl(agree, informative, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n)$p.value), direction = dir)
}

# common abbreviations of condition names, for column and point labels (spelled out in the captions)
abbreviations <- c("Alzheimer's disease" = "AD", "Autism spectrum disorder" = "ASD", "Colorectal cancer" = "CRC",
                   "Dry eye syndrome" = "Dry eye", "Gastric cancer" = "GC", "Head and neck cancer" = "HNC",
                   "HIV infection" = "HIV", "Parkinson's disease" = "PD", "Rheumatoid arthritis" = "RA",
                   "Schizophrenia" = "SCZ", "Smoking behavior" = "Smoking", "Type I diabetes mellitus" = "T1D",
                   "Ulcerative colitis" = "UC", "Unipolar depression" = "MDD")
abbrev <- \(x) coalesce(unname(abbreviations[x]), x)
# short column labels of the direction heatmap, as in paper Figure 4A: "CRC (9/9)", "COVID-19 gut (3/4)"
short_column <- function(col) {
  col <- as.character(col)
  condition <- str_remove(col, " \\(\\d+/\\d+\\)$")
  ifelse(col == "All BugSigDB", col,
         paste(abbrev(str_remove(condition, " \\(\\w+\\)$")), coalesce(str_match(condition, "\\((\\w+)\\)$")[, 2], ""),
               str_extract(col, "\\(\\d+/\\d+\\)$")) |> str_squish())
}

# share reported increased in the combined direction heatmap, as in paper Figure 4A: grey strictly between 1/3 and
# 2/3, where neither direction reaches agree_cut; the colour steps to light blue or orange at the cut-offs
share_colours <- c("#1c5cab", "#2a78d6", "#a9c8ee", "#e3e1dd", "#e3e1dd", "#f5b796", "#eb6834", "#c2410c")
share_values <- c(0, 0.15, 1 / 3, 1 / 3 + 1e-6, 2 / 3 - 1e-6, 2 / 3, 0.85, 1)
scale_fill_share <- function(...) {
  scale_fill_gradientn(colours = share_colours, values = share_values, limits = c(0, 1), na.value = "white", ...)
}
few_grey <- "grey74"

# cells of one genus group of the direction heatmap: one row per genus and column
direction_cells <- function(dir, columns, min_sigs = 5, neutral = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  tests <- direction_tests(dir, min_sigs)
  baseline <- direction_hits(dir) |>
    count_directions() |>
    direction_test(dir) |>
    mutate(Condition = "All BugSigDB")

  bind_rows(baseline, filter(tests, Condition %in% columns$Condition)) |>
    right_join(tidyr::expand_grid(Condition = columns$Condition, taxon = top$taxon),
               by = c("Condition", "taxon")) |>
    left_join(select(columns, Condition, col, block), by = "Condition") |>
    mutate(
      significant = !is.na(fdr) & fdr < 0.05,
      # too few signatures to show a direction
      few = !is.na(n) & n < 3,
      # colour: share reported in the genus group's periodontitis direction (increased: orange, decreased: blue)
      # neutral (combined figure): share reported increased for both genus groups, one key
      share_plot = ifelse(few, NA, if (neutral && dir == "decreased") 1 - share_same else share_same),
      label = ifelse(!is.na(n) & !few, paste0(same, "/", n), ""),
      # mixed: neither direction reaches agree_cut, so the genus is left out of the condition's count
      mixed = Condition != "All BugSigDB" & !is.na(n) & n >= 3 & same / n < agree_cut & same / n > 1 - agree_cut
    )
}

direction_heat_panel <- function(dir, columns, min_sigs = 5, show_x = TRUE, neutral = FALSE) {
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  cells <- direction_cells(dir, columns, min_sigs, neutral)

  # line next to All BugSigDB (after it, or before it when the columns are mirrored)
  all_pos <- columns |>
    mutate(pos = dense_rank(as.integer(col)), n_block = n(), .by = block) |>
    filter(Condition == "All BugSigDB") |>
    mutate(xintercept = ifelse(pos == 1, 1.5, pos - 0.5))
  fill_scale <- if (neutral) {
    scale_fill_share(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), labels = c("All decreased", "Mixed", "All increased"),
                     name = "Studies reporting\nthe genus")
  } else {
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = if (dir == "increased") "#1c5cab" else "#c2410c", mid = "#f0efec",
                         high = if (dir == "increased") "#c2410c" else "#1c5cab", midpoint = 0.5,
                         limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent, na.value = "white",
                         name = paste0("Share of studies\nreporting it ", dir))
  }

  ggplot(cells, aes(x = col, y = factor(taxon, levels = rev(top$taxon)), fill = share_plot)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, few), fill = few_grey, color = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_tile(data = filter(cells, significant), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.7, width = 0.9, height = 0.85) +
    geom_vline(data = select(all_pos, block, xintercept), aes(xintercept = xintercept),
               color = "grey20", linewidth = 0.6) +
    # conditions going the opposite way in a separate panel
    facet_grid(. ~ block, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
    geom_text(aes(label = label, fontface = ifelse(significant, "bold", "plain")), size = 2.4, color = "grey15") +
    fill_scale +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = short_column) +
    guides(fill = guide_colourbar(order = 1)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = if (show_x) element_text(angle = 40, hjust = 1) else element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = if (show_x) element_line() else element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_blank(), strip.background = element_blank(),
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.3, "cm"),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
}

# conditions shown in a direction heatmap: at least min_genera genera with a clear direction, of which
# at least min_agree agree with periodontitis or at least min_agree go the opposite way
direction_conditions <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3, min_genera = 4, min_agree = agree_cut) {
  direction_agreement(dir, min_sigs, min_reports) |>
    filter(informative >= min_genera, agree / informative >= min_agree | against / informative >= min_agree) |>
    mutate(agreeing = agree / informative >= min_agree, k = ifelse(agreeing, agree, against))
}

# body site subsets that are shown, judged over both genus groups: where at least two subsets (body site
# groups) of a condition meet the thresholds, or one does and the whole condition does not. They then replace
# the whole condition, which would pool sites that can go different ways. A single passing subset of a passing
# condition mostly repeats it (e.g. colorectal cancer and its gut studies), so only the whole condition is shown.
shown_subsets <- function(min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3, min_genera = 4, min_agree = agree_cut) {
  passing <- map_dfr(c("increased", "decreased"),
                     \(d) direction_conditions(d, min_sigs, min_reports, min_genera, min_agree))
  site_subsets |>
    filter(subset %in% passing$Condition) |>
    filter(n_distinct(subset) >= 2 | !Condition %in% passing$Condition, .by = Condition) |>
    pull(subset)
}

# one genus group per figure: unlike the other figures (shared core set), each shows the tested
# conditions with at least min_genera genera reported by at least min_reports studies of which at least
# min_agree have more than half of their reports in the periodontitis direction (agreeing, first) or at
# least min_agree in the opposite direction (opposite, after a dashed line), each block ordered by the
# sign test (two-sided against half, as in the next figure), smallest p first. Cells keep the width of
# a figure with n_ref columns, so the heatmap is narrower rather than stretched.
direction_heatmap <- function(dir, min_sigs = 5, min_reports = 3, min_genera = 4, min_agree = agree_cut, n_ref = 13,
                              columns_only = FALSE) {
  condition_sizes <- sigs_with_subsets() |>
    summarise(signatures = n(), oral = mean(oral), .by = Condition)
  # the conditions that meet the thresholds; where two or more of a condition's body site subsets meet them,
  # those subsets instead of the whole condition
  split <- shown_subsets(min_sigs, min_reports, min_genera, min_agree)
  split_conditions <- site_subsets$Condition[site_subsets$subset %in% split]
  conditions <- direction_conditions(dir, min_sigs, min_reports, min_genera, min_agree) |>
    filter(if_else(Condition %in% site_subsets$subset, Condition %in% split, !Condition %in% split_conditions)) |>
    arrange(desc(agreeing), p, desc(k / informative)) |>
    left_join(condition_sizes, by = "Condition")
  columns <- bind_rows(
    tibble(Condition = "All BugSigDB", signatures = nrow(bsdb_sigs), oral = mean(bsdb_sigs$oral)),
    select(conditions, Condition, signatures, oral, agree, against, informative, mixed, agreeing)
  ) |>
    # label: genera agreeing (left panel) or going the opposite way (right panel) / genera with a clear
    # direction (mixed genera, grey in the combined figure, are left out)
    mutate(col = ifelse(is.na(informative), "All BugSigDB",
                        paste0(Condition, " (", ifelse(agreeing, agree, against), "/", informative, ")")),
           col = factor(col, levels = col),
           # All BugSigDB and agreeing conditions in one panel, opposite conditions in another
           block = factor(ifelse(agreeing %in% FALSE, "opposite", "same"), levels = c("same", "opposite")),
           block = droplevels(block))

  if (columns_only) return(columns)
  top <- filter(perio_genera, direction == dir)
  k <- min(nrow(columns) / n_ref, 1)
  (plot_spacer() + oral_panel(columns) + plot_spacer() +
     perio_panel(top, rev(top$taxon)) + direction_heat_panel(dir, columns, min_sigs) + plot_spacer()) +
    plot_layout(ncol = 3, widths = c(1.8, 6 * k, max(6 * (1 - k), 0.01)), heights = c(1, 7))
}

# both genus groups in one figure: periodontitis-increased genera and their heatmap on the left,
# periodontitis-decreased on the right, each with the genus names and PerioSigDB bars on its left,
# separated by a vertical line; one colour key (share reported increased) for both
direction_heatmap_combined <- function(min_sigs = 5) {
  cols_inc <- direction_heatmap("increased", columns_only = TRUE)
  cols_dec <- direction_heatmap("decreased", columns_only = TRUE)
  top_inc <- filter(perio_genera, direction == "increased")
  top_dec <- filter(perio_genera, direction == "decreased")
  separator <- ggplot() +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.6) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 1)) +
    theme_void()
  # title over each half, left-aligned with the genus names (full area, including the axis-label space)
  title <- function(text) {
    wrap_elements(full = grid::textGrob(text, x = 0, hjust = 0,
                                        gp = grid::gpar(fontface = "bold", fontsize = 10.5)))
  }
  no_y <- theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.title.y = element_blank())
  wrap_plots(
    A = title("Periodontitis-increased genera"), B = title("Periodontitis-decreased genera"),
    C = oral_panel(cols_inc), D = oral_panel(cols_dec) + no_y,
    E = perio_panel(top_inc, rev(top_inc$taxon), details = FALSE),
    F = direction_heat_panel("increased", cols_inc, min_sigs, neutral = TRUE),
    S = separator,
    H = perio_panel(top_dec, rev(top_dec$taxon), details = FALSE),
    G = direction_heat_panel("decreased", cols_dec, min_sigs, neutral = TRUE),
    design = "AASBB\n#CS#D\nEFSHG"
  ) +
    plot_layout(widths = c(1.4, nrow(cols_inc) + 0.4, 0.4, 1.4, nrow(cols_dec) + 0.4),
                heights = c(0.25, 1, 7), guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
}

# whole-signature similarity (see "Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis")
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.R (takes ~20 minutes)
semsim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_semantic_similarity.rds")
# Lin similarity of each BugSigDB taxon to the consensus taxa, with taxon lineages
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.R
taxon_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_taxon_similarity.rds")

# similarity of a set of BugSigDB study units to a PerioSigDB consensus, compared with the units of all *other*
# conditions (periodontitis studies are not in bsdb_cc): one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum (Mann-Whitney) test,
# more similar than the background. Shown rank of a unit: share of background units it is more similar than
# (ties count half), so a set's mean rank is U / (n_x * n_y) (0.5 = typical).
# scores: one row per unit and periodontitis consensus (perio), with unit, Condition, direction, site_group, sim.
# Sets, each needing >= min_units units of the BugSigDB direction:
#   all:      all of a condition's units, vs all other units of the direction
#   site_all: a condition's units from one body site group, vs all other units of the direction
#   site:     the same, vs other units of the direction from that site group; only where that site group has
#             >= min_bg_units such units from >= min_bg_conditions other conditions (a proper background)
# BH within each kind of set and each BugSigDB direction x consensus column.
similarity_tests <- function(scores, min_units = 5, min_bg_units = 20, min_bg_conditions = 10) {
  unit_info <- distinct(scores, unit, Condition, direction, site_group)
  sim <- pivot_wider(select(scores, unit, perio, sim), names_from = perio, values_from = sim)
  sim_of <- \(u, pr) sim[[pr]][match(u, sim$unit)]
  rank_vs <- \(x, y) vapply(x, \(v) mean(y < v) + 0.5 * mean(y == v), numeric(1))
  background <- \(cond, dir, kind, s) with(unit_info, unit[direction == dir & Condition != cond &
                                                             (kind != "site" | site_group == s)])
  sets <- bind_rows(mutate(unit_info, kind = "all", site = NA_character_),
                    mutate(unit_info, kind = "site_all", site = site_group),
                    mutate(unit_info, kind = "site", site = site_group)) |>
    filter(n() >= min_units, .by = c(kind, Condition, site, direction)) |>
    nest(units = c(unit, site_group), .by = c(kind, Condition, site, direction)) |>
    mutate(bg = pmap(list(Condition, direction, kind, site), background),
           bg_conditions = map_int(bg, \(b) n_distinct(unit_info$Condition[match(b, unit_info$unit)]))) |>
    filter(kind != "site" | (lengths(bg) >= min_bg_units & bg_conditions >= min_bg_conditions))
  res <- cross_join(sets, tibble(perio = c("increased", "decreased"))) |>
    mutate(x = map2(units, perio, \(u, pr) sim_of(u$unit, pr)),
           y = map2(bg, perio, sim_of),
           ranks = map2(x, y, rank_vs),
           studies = lengths(x), background = lengths(y),
           mean_rank = map_dbl(ranks, mean),
           ci = map_dbl(ranks, \(r) 1.96 * sd(r) / sqrt(length(r))),
           p = map2_dbl(x, y, \(x, y) wilcox.test(x, y, alternative = "greater", exact = FALSE)$p.value)) |>
    mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = c(kind, direction, perio))
  list(stats = select(res, kind, Condition, site, direction, perio, studies, background, bg_conditions,
                      mean_rank, ci, p, fdr),
       units = res |> mutate(units = map2(units, ranks, \(u, r) mutate(u, rank = r))) |>
         select(kind, Condition, site, direction, perio, units) |> unnest(units))
}

# mean best-match similarity of each study unit to the two consensus signatures, over its signatures with
# at least 5 taxa (as in the BugSigDB paper): smaller ones give extreme, noisy similarities
semsim_scores <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(lengths(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig]) >= 5) |>
  inner_join(semsim$similarity, by = c("bsdb_id" = "BSDB ID")) |>
  summarise(increased = mean(sim_increased), decreased = mean(sim_decreased),
            .by = c(unit, Condition, direction, site_group)) |>
  pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "perio", values_to = "sim")
semsim_tests <- similarity_tests(semsim_scores)

# assay type of a signature's profiling method (targeted-panel check, consistency check rows)
assay_of <- \(m) case_when(m %in% c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics") ~ "Sequencing",
                           m %in% c("PCR", "DNA-DNA hybridization") ~ "Targeted",
                           .default = "Other / not reported")
```

PerioSigDB uses BugSigDB's format, so its signatures can be compared with signatures from other microbiome studies. These analyses use the BugSigDB export of `r bsdb_version`, with `r n_distinct(bsdb$PMID)` studies and `r nrow(bsdb)` signatures across all conditions and body sites. BugSigDB's own periodontitis signatures (`r nrow(bsdb) - nrow(bsdb_other)`) are excluded throughout.

## Profiling methods and taxonomic resolution

```{r bsdb-methods}
#| fig-width: 13
#| fig-height: 3.8
#| fig-cap: "Profiling method and taxonomic resolution of PerioSigDB and BugSigDB signatures. (A) Profiling method of signatures (share of signatures). (B) Taxonomic rank of the taxa in signatures, counting each taxon once for every signature that lists it. BugSigDB includes all conditions and body sites except periodontitis."

method_of <- function(type, platform) {
  case_when(
    type == "16S" ~ "16S rRNA sequencing",
    type == "WMS" ~ "Shotgun metagenomics",
    type %in% c("PCR", "16S,PCR") ~ "PCR",
    platform == "DNA-DNA Hybridization" ~ "DNA-DNA hybridization",
    .default = "Other / not reported"
  ) |>
    factor(levels = method_levels)
}

methods_db <- bind_rows(
  dat |> transmute(db = "PerioSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`)),
  bsdb_other |> transmute(db = "BugSigDB", method = method_of(`Sequencing type`, `Sequencing platform`))
) |>
  count(db, method) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

rank_names <- c(s = "Species", g = "Genus", f = "Family", o = "Order", c = "Class", p = "Phylum", k = "Kingdom")
pal_rank <- c(Species = "#184f95", Genus = "#3987e5", Family = "#86b6ef", Higher = "#cde2fb")

ranks_db <- bind_rows(
  tibble(db = "PerioSigDB", taxon = unlist(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`)),
  tibble(db = "BugSigDB", taxon = unlist(bsdb_other$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`))
) |>
  mutate(
    rank = rank_names[substr(sub(".*[|]", "", taxon), 1, 1)],
    rank = factor(ifelse(rank %in% c("Species", "Genus", "Family"), rank, "Higher"), levels = names(pal_rank))
  ) |>
  count(db, rank) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), db = factor(db, levels = rev(db_levels)), .by = db)

# short method names in the legend, as in paper Figure 3B
method_short <- setNames(c("16S rRNA", "Shotgun", "DNA–DNA hybridization", "PCR", "Other / not reported"), method_levels)

stack_bar <- function(d, fill, pal, tag, labels = names(pal)) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = prop, y = db, fill = {{ fill }})) +
    geom_col(color = "white", linewidth = 0.5, position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE), width = 0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(prop >= 0.07, scales::percent(prop, 1), "")),
              position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5, reverse = TRUE), color = "white", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal, labels = labels) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, expand = c(0, 0)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, tag = tag) +
    guides(fill = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
}

# shares quoted in the text
rank_pct <- \(d, r) scales::percent(sum(ranks_db$prop[ranks_db$db == d & ranks_db$rank %in% r]), 1)
method_pct <- \(d, m) scales::percent(sum(methods_db$prop[methods_db$db == d & methods_db$method %in% m]), 1)

stack_bar(methods_db, method, pal_method, "A", labels = method_short) +
  stack_bar(ranks_db, rank, pal_rank, "B") +
  plot_layout(widths = c(1.3, 1))
```
