`r method_pct("PerioSigDB", c("PCR", "DNA-DNA hybridization"))` of PerioSigDB signatures come from targeted PCR or hybridization, and `r rank_pct("PerioSigDB", "Species")` of their taxa are species. `r method_pct("BugSigDB", c("16S rRNA sequencing", "Shotgun metagenomics"))` of BugSigDB signatures come from sequencing, and more of their taxa are genera (`r rank_pct("BugSigDB", "Genus")`) than species (`r rank_pct("BugSigDB", "Species")`). A bacterium that PerioSigDB names as a species often appears in BugSigDB only as its genus. Signatures from the two databases are therefore comparable at genus level. The genus analyses below count each taxon as its genus and leave out taxa above genus rank. The similarity analyses instead compare taxa through the NCBI taxonomy, so they keep every rank.

## How consistent are signatures across studies?

How well do one condition's signatures from different studies agree? The BugSigDB paper ranked conditions by this agreement (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 2) and found antibiotics and HIV infection the most consistent. Here periodontitis (PerioSigDB) is placed among the BugSigDB conditions. Oral signatures share many taxa, so each condition is compared with random signatures from the same body sites, drawn from the signatures of all other conditions. The figure shows the 10 conditions per direction whose studies agree most beyond random, with periodontitis and three checks on it.

```{r replicability}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-cap: "The 10 conditions per direction with the most consistent signatures across studies, and periodontitis. Point: mean taxonomic similarity between the condition's signatures from different studies, with each pair of studies counted once. Similarity is the best-match average of Lin similarity, over signatures with at least 5 taxa. Grey bar and tick: central 95% and mean of the same score for 1,000 random sets of signatures. These come from all other conditions, matched to the condition in number, direction and body site group. Rows are ordered by how far the score exceeds the random mean; brackets give the number of studies. Filled: FDR < 0.05 (one-sided resampling test, Benjamini–Hochberg across all conditions tested in that direction). Green: periodontitis, and its signatures from sequencing (16S and shotgun) or targeted assays (PCR and checkerboard hybridization) only. Blue: BugSigDB signatures from dental plaque, pooled across conditions. Their random sets come from all other oral signatures of the direction. The assay and plaque rows check periodontitis's agreement. They are ranked like the other rows and filled at unadjusted p < 0.05."
# precomputed by scripts/bugsigdb_replicability.R
rep_sim <- readRDS("../../output/bugsigdb_replicability_sim.rds")

rep_sigs <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = paste0("perio:", dat$perio_row), Study = dat$Study, Condition = "Periodontitis",
         direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`, site_group = "oral"),
  tibble(id = bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`, Study = bsdb_cc$Study, Condition = bsdb_cc$Condition,
         direction = bsdb_cc$`Abundance in Group 1`, site_group = site_group(bsdb_cc$`Body site`))
) |>
  filter(id %in% rownames(rep_sim)) |>
  mutate(pos = match(id, rownames(rep_sim)))

# mean similarity between different studies, each pair of studies counting once: similarities are
# averaged over the two studies' signatures, then over pairs of studies
cross_study_sim <- function(idx) {
  study <- rep_sigs$Study[idx]
  s <- rep_sim[rep_sigs$pos[idx], rep_sigs$pos[idx]]
  sums <- rowsum(t(rowsum(s, study)), study)
  n <- as.vector(table(study)[rownames(sums)])
  means <- sums / outer(n, n)
  mean(means[upper.tri(means)])
}

# observed score vs random sets of signatures of *other* conditions with the same direction and site groups
set.seed(1)
replicability <- rep_sigs |>
  mutate(i = row_number()) |>
  filter(n_distinct(Study) >= 5, .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  summarise(studies = n_distinct(Study), idx = list(i), .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  mutate(
    observed = map_dbl(idx, cross_study_sim),
    random = pmap(list(idx, Condition, direction), \(idx, cond, dir) {
      # the pool excludes the condition's own signatures, so the question is whether its studies agree more
      # than studies of other conditions from the same site groups (as in the whole-signature similarity tests)
      other <- rep_sigs$direction == dir & rep_sigs$Condition != cond
      pool <- split(which(other), rep_sigs$site_group[other])
      need <- table(rep_sigs$site_group[idx])
      # site groups with fewer signatures than needed are drawn from all other signatures of this direction
      draw <- \(g) {
        from <- if (!is.null(pool[[g]]) && length(pool[[g]]) >= need[[g]]) pool[[g]] else unlist(pool)
        from[sample.int(length(from), need[[g]])]
      }
      r <- replicate(1000, cross_study_sim(unlist(map(names(need), draw))))
      r[!is.na(r)]
    }),
    random_mean = map_dbl(random, mean),
    lo = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.025), hi = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.975),
    p = map2_dbl(observed, random, \(o, r) (1 + sum(r >= o)) / (1 + length(r))),
    excess = observed - random_mean
  ) |>
  mutate(fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"), .by = direction)

# the same test on subsets of the periodontitis signatures, and on BugSigDB's plaque signatures
rep_perio <- rep_sigs |> filter(Condition == "Periodontitis")
rep_assay <- assay_of(method_of(dat$`Sequencing type`, dat$`Sequencing platform`))[
  match(as.integer(sub("perio:", "", rep_perio$id)), dat$perio_row)]
rep_plaque <- rep_sigs |>
  filter(Condition != "Periodontitis", site_group == "oral") |>
  filter(grepl("plaque", bsdb_cc$`Body site`[match(id, bsdb_cc$`BSDB ID`)], ignore.case = TRUE))

rep_subsets <- bind_rows(
  rep_sigs,
  mutate(rep_perio[rep_assay == "Sequencing", ], Condition = "Periodontitis (sequencing only)"),
  mutate(rep_perio[rep_assay == "Targeted", ], Condition = "Periodontitis (targeted only)"),
  mutate(filter(rep_sigs, id %in% rep_plaque$id), Condition = "BugSigDB dental plaque")
)
subset_sim <- function(idx) {
  study <- rep_subsets$Study[idx]
  s <- rep_sim[rep_subsets$pos[idx], rep_subsets$pos[idx]]
  sums <- rowsum(t(rowsum(s, study)), study)
  n <- as.vector(table(study)[rownames(sums)])
  means <- sums / outer(n, n)
  mean(means[upper.tri(means)])
}
subset_levels <- c("Periodontitis", "Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "Periodontitis (targeted only)",
                   "BugSigDB dental plaque")
set.seed(1)
rep_sens <- rep_subsets |>
  mutate(i = row_number()) |>
  filter(Condition %in% subset_levels) |>
  summarise(studies = n_distinct(Study), idx = list(i), .by = c(Condition, direction)) |>
  mutate(
    observed = map_dbl(idx, subset_sim),
    random = pmap(list(idx, Condition, direction), \(idx, cond, dir) {
      # periodontitis subsets keep the published pool (all other conditions, matched on site group);
      # the plaque row is compared with all other oral signatures of the direction
      other <- if (cond == "BugSigDB dental plaque") {
        rep_subsets$direction == dir & rep_subsets$site_group == "oral" &
          !rep_subsets$Condition %in% subset_levels
      } else {
        rep_subsets$direction == dir & !grepl("^Periodontitis", rep_subsets$Condition) &
          rep_subsets$Condition != "BugSigDB dental plaque"
      }
      pool <- split(which(other), rep_subsets$site_group[other])
      need <- table(rep_subsets$site_group[idx])
      draw <- \(g) {
        from <- if (!is.null(pool[[g]]) && length(pool[[g]]) >= need[[g]]) pool[[g]] else unlist(pool)
        from[sample.int(length(from), need[[g]])]
      }
      r <- replicate(1000, subset_sim(unlist(map(names(need), draw))))
      r[!is.na(r)]
    }),
    random_mean = map_dbl(random, mean), lo = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.025),
    hi = map_dbl(random, quantile, 0.975),
    p = map2_dbl(observed, random, \(o, r) (1 + sum(r >= o)) / (1 + length(r)))
  )

# the 10 conditions per direction with the largest excess, plus periodontitis if outside them (FDR stays
# computed over all conditions), and the checks, all ranked by excess
check_labels <- c("Periodontitis (sequencing only)" = "Periodontitis: sequencing",
                  "Periodontitis (targeted only)" = "Periodontitis: targeted",
                  "BugSigDB dental plaque" = "Dental plaque, pooled")
rep_rows <- bind_rows(
  replicability |>
    filter(rank(-excess) <= 10 | Condition == "Periodontitis", .by = direction) |>
    mutate(kind = ifelse(Condition == "Periodontitis", "perio", "condition"), filled = fdr < 0.05,
           label = Condition, key = excess),
  rep_sens |>
    filter(Condition %in% names(check_labels)) |>
    mutate(kind = ifelse(Condition == "BugSigDB dental plaque", "plaque", "perio"), filled = p < 0.05,
           label = check_labels[Condition], key = observed - random_mean)) |>
  mutate(direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in the condition", "Decreased in the condition")),
         label = paste0(label, " (", studies, ")"),
         row = fct_reorder(paste(label, direction, sep = "___"), key))

# values quoted in the text
rep_all <- bind_rows(replicability, filter(rep_sens, Condition != "Periodontitis"))
rep_get <- \(cond, dir, col) rep_all[[col]][rep_all$Condition == cond & rep_all$direction == dir]
rep_num <- \(cond, dir, col) sprintf("%.2f", rep_get(cond, dir, col))
rep_p <- \(cond, dir, col = "p") signif(rep_get(cond, dir, col), 1)
# rank by excess among the BugSigDB conditions and periodontitis (with one subset in place of periodontitis)
rep_rank <- \(cond, dir) {
  r <- filter(replicability, direction == dir, Condition != "Periodontitis")
  1 + sum(r$excess > rep_get(cond, dir, "observed") - rep_get(cond, dir, "random_mean"))
}
n_rep <- \(dir) sum(replicability$direction == dir)

ggplot(rep_rows, aes(y = row)) +
  # shading drawn on every row (transparent for most), as a filtered layer would reorder the rows
  geom_tile(aes(x = 0), width = Inf, height = 1,
            fill = c(perio = "#dff3ea", plaque = "#e6eef8", condition = NA)[rep_rows$kind]) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0, linewidth = 2.5, color = "grey85") +
  geom_point(aes(x = random_mean), shape = "|", size = 3, color = "grey45") +
  geom_point(aes(x = observed, fill = filled), shape = 21, size = 2.8, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey10", `FALSE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_y_discrete(labels = \(x) sub("___.*", "", x)) +
  # panel titles as in paper Figure 3D
  facet_wrap(~direction, scales = "free_y",
             labeller = as_labeller(c("Increased in the condition" = "Increased signatures",
                                      "Decreased in the condition" = "Decreased signatures"))) +
  labs(x = "Mean similarity between signatures from different studies", y = NULL) +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

Periodontitis's increased signatures agree between studies more than site-matched random sets do (`r rep_num("Periodontitis", "increased", "observed")` vs `r rep_num("Periodontitis", "increased", "random_mean")`, FDR = `r rep_p("Periodontitis", "increased", "fdr")`), rank `r rep_rank("Periodontitis", "increased")` of `r n_rep("increased")` conditions. Sequencing and targeted signatures each agree more than random sets on their own. BugSigDB's own plaque signatures are no more alike than random ones, so neither fixed panels nor plaque sampling explain it.

All the decreased signatures together agree only slightly more than random (FDR = `r rep_p("Periodontitis", "decreased", "fdr")`). The sequencing signatures alone agree clearly (`r rep_num("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased", "observed")` vs `r rep_num("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased", "random_mean")`, p = `r rep_p("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased")`), which would rank `r rep_rank("Periodontitis (sequencing only)", "decreased")` of `r n_rep("decreased")` conditions. Only `r rep_get("Periodontitis (targeted only)", "decreased", "studies")` targeted studies report decreased taxa, and they agree no more than random. Pooling them with the sequencing studies dilutes the overall agreement.

## Periodontitis-associated genera in other conditions

In which other conditions does the microbiome literature (BugSigDB) report the taxa that PerioSigDB links to periodontitis? The analysis uses only BugSigDB's human disease-vs-control comparisons and leaves out meta-analyses (`r nrow(bsdb_cc)` signatures from `r n_distinct(bsdb_cc$Study)` studies). Each study counts once per condition, direction and body site group. The body site groups are oral (mouth, saliva, dental plaque, tongue, gums, inner cheek, lip), upper airway (throat, pharynx including the oropharynx, nose), lower airway, gastrointestinal, urogenital, skin, eye and other (e.g. blood, milk). Signatures that list sites from several groups count as mixed. Condition labels that name the same condition are merged (e.g. colorectal carcinoma into colorectal cancer; oral, pharyngeal and laryngeal cancers into head and neck cancer).

A condition can be compared only if BugSigDB has enough studies of it, and the clinically nearest conditions fall short. Every test here needs 5 study units, but BugSigDB has 2 gingivitis units per direction and 1 each for peri-implantitis, dental caries and halitosis. "The condition most like periodontitis" therefore means the most similar among conditions with enough studies, which are mostly gut conditions and cancers.

### Do sequencing studies alone find the same genera?

Half of PerioSigDB signatures come from checkerboard DNA–DNA hybridization and PCR, which detect only the taxa on a fixed panel. The panels were designed around taxa already suspected in periodontitis. If these studies drove the binomial test, the periodontitis-associated genera would reflect panel design rather than disease. Repeating the test on sequencing signatures alone shows which genera these studies still find.

```{r assay-genera}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-associated genera from all PerioSigDB signatures (left) and from sequencing signatures only (16S and shotgun; right). Rows: genera with unadjusted p < 0.05 in either analysis, grouped by periodontitis direction. Test: exact binomial test of increased vs decreased signatures against 50%. Rows are ordered by the all-signatures p, with genera significant only with sequencing at the bottom of their group. Bars: signatures reporting the genus increased (right) or decreased (left), on the same scale in both columns. Solid: FDR < 0.05 (Benjamini–Hochberg across all genera tested in that analysis). Faded: p < 0.05 only. Grey: p ≥ 0.05. Numbers: unadjusted p."
sig_assay <- tibble(sig = seq_len(nrow(dat)),
                    method = method_of(dat$`Sequencing type`, dat$`Sequencing platform`)) |>
  mutate(assay = assay_of(method))
genus_assay <- sig_genera(dat) |> left_join(sig_assay, by = "sig")

# the same binomial test on sequencing signatures only
seq_tests <- genus_assay |>
  filter(assay == "Sequencing") |>
  count_directions() |>
  mutate(signatures = increased + decreased,
         p = map2_dbl(increased, signatures, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
         fdr = p.adjust(p, method = "BH"),
         direction = case_when(increased > decreased ~ "increased", decreased > increased ~ "decreased"))

# rows: genera with p < 0.05 in either analysis, in their direction in that analysis; ordered by the
# all-signatures p, with genera significant only with sequencing at the bottom of their group
assay_analyses <- c(all = "All signatures", seq = "Sequencing only (16S, shotgun)")
assay_tests <- bind_rows(all = perio_tests, seq = seq_tests, .id = "analysis") |>
  select(analysis, taxon, increased, decreased, p, fdr, direction)
assay_rows <- assay_tests |>
  filter(p < 0.05, !is.na(direction)) |>
  arrange(analysis != "all", p, desc(increased + decreased)) |>
  distinct(taxon, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  select(taxon, row_dir = direction)
dir_label <- c(increased = "Increased in periodontitis", decreased = "Decreased in periodontitis")
assay_cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(assay_rows, analysis = names(assay_analyses)) |>
  left_join(assay_tests, by = c("taxon", "analysis")) |>
  mutate(status = case_when(is.na(p) ~ "not reported", fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05", p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05",
                            .default = "p ≥ 0.05"),
         across(c(increased, decreased), \(x) replace_na(x, 0L)),
         p_label = case_when(is.na(p) ~ "–", p < 0.001 ~ "<0.001", .default = sprintf("%.3f", p)),
         taxon = factor(taxon, levels = rev(assay_rows$taxon)),
         row_dir = factor(dir_label[row_dir], levels = dir_label),
         analysis = factor(assay_analyses[analysis], levels = assay_analyses))
assay_bars <- assay_cells |>
  pivot_longer(c(increased, decreased), names_to = "sig_direction", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(n = ifelse(sig_direction == "decreased", -n, n),
         fill = ifelse(status %in% c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05"), sig_direction, "ns"))
max_assay <- max(abs(assay_bars$n))

fig_s5 <- ggplot(assay_bars, aes(n, taxon)) +
  geom_col(aes(fill = fill, alpha = status), width = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "grey30", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_text(data = assay_cells, aes(x = -max_assay * 0.5, label = p_label,
                                    color = status %in% c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05")),
            hjust = 1, size = 2.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(increased = "#eb6834", decreased = "#2a78d6", ns = "grey70"),
                    breaks = c("increased", "decreased"),
                    labels = c("Signatures reporting increased", "Signatures reporting decreased"), name = NULL) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`FDR < 0.05` = 1, `p < 0.05` = 0.45, `p ≥ 0.05` = 1, `not reported` = 1),
                     guide = "none") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "grey20", `FALSE` = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = abs, limits = c(-max_assay * 0.72, max_assay * 1.03),
                     breaks = c(-25, 0, 25, 50, 75)) +
  facet_grid(row_dir ~ analysis, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus", y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "top")
# counts quoted in the text
n_genera <- \(d) sum(perio_genera$direction == d)
seq_recovered <- \(d) length(intersect(perio_genera$taxon[perio_genera$direction == d],
                                       seq_tests$taxon[seq_tests$p < 0.05 & seq_tests$direction %in% d]))
fig_s5
```

Sequencing signatures alone recover `r seq_recovered("increased")` of the `r n_genera("increased")` increased and `r seq_recovered("decreased")` of the `r n_genera("decreased")` decreased genera, so most of the genera do not depend on panel studies. *Campylobacter* rests on panel studies: sequencing studies report it increased and decreased about equally often. *Selenomonas* and *Alloprevotella* among the increased genera, and *Bergeyella* and *Kingella* among the decreased, keep their direction in sequencing studies but have too few signatures to reach p < 0.05.

### Which conditions report these genera in the same direction as periodontitis?

The direction heatmap shows, for each genus group, the conditions whose studies most often report these genera in the periodontitis direction, and those that most often report them the opposite way.

```{r bsdb-direction-combined}
#| fig-width: 15
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-associated genera and the direction other conditions report them in (BugSigDB). Left: the 19 periodontitis-increased genera. Right: the 12 periodontitis-decreased genera (binomial p < 0.05). Bars beside the genus names: PerioSigDB signatures reporting the genus decreased (left) or increased (right). They are coloured and shaded as in the consensus taxa figure. Faded: not significant after Benjamini–Hochberg correction; palest: unadjusted p ≥ 0.05. Columns on each side start with all of BugSigDB, next to the genus names. Then come the conditions with at least 4 of these genera that have a clear direction, each reported by at least 3 of their studies. In the first panel at least two thirds of these genera agree with periodontitis. In the second at least two thirds go the opposite way. Each panel is ordered by a two-sided sign test of that count against half, smallest p first. Conditions are also tested on their studies from one body site group alone, such as COVID-19 gut, with the same criteria. A condition's subsets are shown where at least two of them meet the criteria, or one does and the whole condition does not (in either genus group). They then replace the whole condition. Otherwise only the whole condition is shown. In brackets: genera agreeing or going the opposite way, out of the genera with a clear direction. Cells: studies reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction / all studies reporting it. The periodontitis direction is increased on the left and decreased on the right. Colour: share of the studies that report the genus increased, from blue (all decreased) to orange (all increased). Light grey: mixed, with between one and two thirds of the studies in the periodontitis direction (e.g. 2 of 4). Mixed genera are left out of the count in brackets. At exactly one or two thirds the colour changes to light blue or light orange. Dark grey: 1–2 studies. White: not reported. Outlined: FDR < 0.05 in a two-sided binomial test of the cell's studies against 50%. An outlined cell can therefore be significant in either direction. Top bars: share of the column's studies from oral sites. CRC: colorectal cancer; GC: gastric cancer; HNC: head and neck cancer; PD: Parkinson's disease; RA: rheumatoid arthritis; Smoking: smoking behavior."
direction_heatmap_combined()
```

Colorectal cancer is the only condition with genera whose direction differs from 50% after correction: *Peptostreptococcus* (25 of 25 studies increased), *Parvimonas* (22/22), *Porphyromonas* (20/21) and *Fusobacterium* (29/34), all as in periodontitis. *Gemella*, decreased in periodontitis, goes the opposite way (15 of 15 increased).

#### Direction summary

This figure summarises each condition over all the periodontitis-associated genera its studies report, with each genus counted once. It shows only the direction of reports, not how often the genera are reported or whether they change together within participants.

```{r bsdb-agreement-map}
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 7.6
#| fig-cap: "Direction of the periodontitis-associated genera in each BugSigDB condition. Genera counted: the periodontitis-associated genera reported by at least 3 of the condition's studies. A genus agrees with periodontitis if at least two thirds of these studies report it in the periodontitis direction. It goes the opposite way if at most one third do. Genera in between (e.g. 2 of 4 studies) have no clear direction and are left out, as in the direction heatmap. x: share of the periodontitis-increased genera with a clear direction that agree (reported increased). y: the same for the periodontitis-decreased genera (reported decreased). Conditions: those shown in the direction heatmap (either genus group). Point size: number of genera counted. Shape: a condition with body site points has its own shape; the other conditions are circles. Colour: the body site group of at least two thirds of the condition's study units (grey: mixed). Shaded area: same direction as periodontitis for both genus groups. Body site points: the body site columns of the direction heatmap, with an arrow from all of the condition's studies to those of the site. COVID-19 and RA are mixed: no site group has two thirds of their units. CRC: colorectal cancer; GC: gastric cancer; HNC: head and neck cancer; PD: Parkinson's disease; RA: rheumatoid arthritis."
# arrows on the 50% lines, pointing outward from the centre; what each direction means is written on the
# top and right axes, outside the panel, so that points near the lines cannot cover it
centre_arrow <- arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), angle = 25, type = "open")
h_arrows <- tibble(xend = c(1.035, -0.035))
v_arrows <- tibble(yend = c(1.035, -0.035))
direction_axes <- function(lo, hi, at) dup_axis(name = NULL, breaks = at, labels = c(paste("←", lo), paste(hi, "→")))
direction_axis_theme <- theme(axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey45", lineheight = 0.9),
                              axis.text.y.right = element_text(size = 8, color = "grey45", lineheight = 0.9,
                                                               angle = 90, hjust = 0.5),
                              axis.ticks.x.top = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y.right = element_blank())

# only the conditions shown in the direction heatmap (either genus group)
heatmap_conditions <- union(direction_conditions("increased")$Condition, direction_conditions("decreased")$Condition)
# body site: the body site columns of the direction heatmap each get a point, with an arrow from all of the
# condition's studies to those of the site
site_names <- c(oral = "mouth", gastrointestinal = "gut", "upper airway" = "airway", "lower airway" = "lung",
                urogenital = "urogenital", skin = "skin", eye = "eye", other = "other", mixed = "mixed sites")
site_points <- agreement_map_site |>
  inner_join(filter(site_subsets, subset %in% shown_subsets()) |> select(Condition, site_group),
             by = c("Condition", "site_group")) |>
  mutate(label = paste0(Condition, " (", site_names[site_group], ")"), site = TRUE)
# one filled shape (triangle, square, diamond, ...) per condition with body site points in this figure; the
# other conditions are circles
site_conditions <- unique(site_points$Condition)
split_shapes <- setNames(c(25, 22, 23, 24)[seq_along(site_conditions)], site_conditions)
unit_site_colours <- c(mouth = "#1b9e77", gut = "#a6761d", airway = "#7570b3", lung = "#e7298a",
                       urogenital = "#66a61e", skin = "#e6ab02", eye = "#1f78b4", other = "grey55",
                       "mixed sites" = "grey30")
# shared with the similarity overview: point colour (the body site group of at least two thirds of the
# units, else mixed)
ov_mixed <- "mixed (no site ≥ 2/3)"
ov_site_colours <- c(unit_site_colours[names(unit_site_colours) != "mixed sites"], setNames("grey60", ov_mixed))
main_site_of <- \(site_group, share) ifelse(share >= 2/3, coalesce(site_names[as.character(site_group)], "other"), ov_mixed)
# main body site of all of a condition's study units (both directions)
condition_main_site <- bsdb_sigs |>
  count(Condition, site_group) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = Condition) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = Condition) |>
  transmute(Condition, main_site = main_site_of(site_group, share))
agreement_plot <- agreement_map |>
  filter(Condition %in% heatmap_conditions) |>
  mutate(site = FALSE) |>
  left_join(condition_main_site, by = "Condition") |>
  # body site points first, so that at tied coordinates they sit on the side their arrow comes from
  (\(d) bind_rows(mutate(site_points, main_site = main_site_of(site_group, rep(1, n()))), d))() |>
  # conditions at identical coordinates are spread slightly sideways so that both are visible
  mutate(plot_x = frac_increased + (row_number() - (n() + 1) / 2) * 0.035, .by = c(frac_increased, frac_decreased)) |>
  mutate(main_site = factor(main_site, levels = names(ov_site_colours)),
         # main point: the condition's abbreviation; body site points: the condition and the site
         label = ifelse(site, paste(abbrev(Condition), site_names[site_group]), abbrev(Condition)),
         shape = coalesce(unname(split_shapes[Condition]), 21))
# arrows from a condition (all studies) to its body site points, shortened to stop short of the points
site_arrows <- inner_join(filter(agreement_plot, !site) |> select(Condition, x = plot_x, y = frac_decreased),
                          filter(agreement_plot, site) |> select(Condition, xend = plot_x, yend = frac_decreased),
                          by = "Condition") |>
  mutate(d = sqrt((xend - x)^2 + (yend - y)^2), gap = pmin(0.1, d * 0.35),
         x0 = x + (xend - x) * 0.05 / d, y0 = y + (yend - y) * 0.05 / d,
         x1 = xend - (xend - x) * gap / d, y1 = yend - (yend - y) * gap / d)
# label data: the points, plus unlabelled points along the arrows (so that labels are pushed off them);
# points on or just below the 50% line get their labels below, off the dashed line
map_labels <- bind_rows(
  agreement_plot |> transmute(plot_x, frac_decreased, label, point_size = 8 * sqrt(genera / max(genera)),
                              text_size = ifelse(site, 2.9, 3.1), face = ifelse(site, "italic", "plain"),
                              text_col = ifelse(site, "grey40", "grey15"),
                              ny = ifelse(abs(frac_decreased - 0.5) < 0.1, -0.08, 0)),
  site_arrows |> mutate(n = pmax(2, ceiling(d / 0.03))) |>
    reframe(t = seq(0.15, 0.85, length.out = n), .by = c(x0, y0, x1, y1, n)) |>
    transmute(plot_x = x0 + (x1 - x0) * t, frac_decreased = y0 + (y1 - y0) * t, label = "", point_size = 1,
              text_size = 2.9, face = "plain", text_col = "grey40", ny = 0))

p_map <- ggplot(agreement_plot, aes(plot_x, frac_decreased)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.5, xmax = 1, ymin = 0.5, ymax = 1, fill = "grey94") +
  # dashed lines, with solid heads at the tips (a dashed arrow draws a broken head)
  geom_segment(data = h_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, xend = xend, y = 0.5, yend = 0.5), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = v_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, xend = 0.5, y = 0.5, yend = yend), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = h_arrows, aes(x = xend - sign(xend - 0.5) * 0.001, xend = xend, y = 0.5, yend = 0.5),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  geom_segment(data = v_arrows, aes(x = 0.5, xend = 0.5, y = yend - sign(yend - 0.5) * 0.001, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  # body site arrows, above the shading
  geom_segment(data = site_arrows, aes(x = x0, y = y0, xend = x1, yend = y1), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               color = "grey35", linewidth = 0.5, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), angle = 25, type = "open")) +
  geom_point(aes(size = genera, fill = main_site, shape = shape), color = "grey15", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_point(aes(size = genera, shape = shape), color = "grey15", fill = NA) +
  scale_shape_identity() +
  # (text size and face set per label outside aes, so that they do not share the point size scale)
  geom_label_repel(data = map_labels, aes(label = label, point.size = point_size),
                   size = map_labels$text_size, fontface = map_labels$face, color = map_labels$text_col,
                   fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.75), linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
                   nudge_y = map_labels$ny, seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.4,
                   point.padding = 0.1, force = 4, segment.color = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3,
                   max.overlaps = Inf, max.iter = 20000, ylim = c(-0.02, 1.02)) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Genera counted") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ov_site_colours, name = "Main body site", drop = TRUE,
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(shape = 21, size = 4, alpha = 1))) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent,
                     sec.axis = direction_axes("Taxa decreased in condition\ninclude perio-increased genera",
                                               "Taxa increased in condition\ninclude perio-increased genera", c(0.25, 0.75))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25),
                     sec.axis = direction_axes("Taxa increased in condition\ninclude perio-decreased genera",
                                               "Taxa decreased in condition\ninclude perio-decreased genera", c(0.25, 0.75))) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-0.05, 1.05), ylim = c(-0.05, 1.05), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Share of periodontitis-increased genera reported increased in the condition",
       y = "Share of periodontitis-decreased genera reported decreased in the condition") +
  theme(legend.position = "top", legend.box = "vertical", legend.box.just = "left",
        legend.title = element_text(size = 9)) +
  direction_axis_theme

# shares quoted in the text
map_pct <- \(cond, col, site_name = NULL) {
  d <- if (is.null(site_name)) agreement_map else site_points[site_points$site_group == site_name, ]
  scales::percent(d[[col]][d$Condition == cond], 1)
}

p_map
```

Head and neck cancer and smoking, both studied mainly in the mouth, sit in the shaded area: their studies report both genus groups in the periodontitis direction. Head and neck cancer agrees for 14 of 16 genera (sign test p = 0.004).

Colorectal cancer, gastric cancer and rheumatoid arthritis agree only for the increased genera. Colorectal cancer studies report `r map_pct("Colorectal cancer", "frac_increased")` of the periodontitis-increased genera increased, but only `r map_pct("Colorectal cancer", "frac_decreased")` of the periodontitis-decreased genera decreased; they report the rest increased too. In these mostly gut studies, oral genera of both groups rise together.

Body site changes the picture within a condition. COVID-19 gut studies report `r map_pct("COVID-19", "frac_increased", "gastrointestinal")` of the periodontitis-increased genera increased and `r map_pct("COVID-19", "frac_decreased", "gastrointestinal")` of the decreased genera decreased, like the gut cancers. Its airway studies report `r map_pct("COVID-19", "frac_increased", "upper airway")` of the increased genera increased. All COVID-19 studies together land between the two, so the pooled position reflects the mix of sites rather than the disease. The sign tests are not corrected across conditions.

### Which genera are less widely reported in other conditions?

The BugSigDB paper proposed genera that several studies report in only one condition as candidate condition-specific markers (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Supplementary Figure). Few periodontitis-associated genera are exclusive, so here each genus's support in PerioSigDB is set against the number of other conditions that report it in the same direction. These counts describe the curated literature, not diagnostic specificity. They depend on how many studies each condition has and which methods those studies used.

```{r specificity}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Periodontitis-associated genera and how many other conditions report them. x: PerioSigDB studies reporting the genus increased (left) or decreased (right) in periodontitis. y: other BugSigDB conditions with at least one study reporting the genus in the same direction. These are human disease-vs-control comparisons from all body sites. Genera: the periodontitis-increased and periodontitis-decreased genera (binomial p < 0.05). Shaded, with coloured points: genera reported by at least 10 PerioSigDB studies and no more than 15 other conditions. The cut-offs describe the data rather than classify genera. The points form a continuum, and moving the cut-offs changes which genera fall inside."
# the periodontitis-associated genera only, each in its consensus direction
perio_support <- sig_genera(dat) |>
  left_join(tibble(sig = seq_len(nrow(dat)), Study = dat$Study), by = "sig") |>
  distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
  count(taxon, direction, name = "perio_studies") |>
  semi_join(perio_genera, by = c("taxon", "direction"))

other_support <- bsdb_genera |>
  left_join(select(bsdb_sigs, sig, Condition, site_group), by = "sig") |>
  summarise(other_conditions = n_distinct(Condition), .by = c(taxon, direction))

specificity <- perio_support |>
  left_join(other_support, by = c("taxon", "direction")) |>
  mutate(other_conditions = coalesce(other_conditions, 0L),
         direction = factor(direction, levels = c("increased", "decreased"),
                            labels = c("Increased in periodontitis", "Decreased in periodontitis")))

# corner (at least 10 PerioSigDB studies, at most 15 other conditions): shaded and its points filled in the
# direction's colour, as in paper Figure S2
spec_corner <- \(d) d$perio_studies >= 10 & d$other_conditions <= 15
spec_light <- c("Increased in periodontitis" = "#fbe3d6", "Decreased in periodontitis" = "#dde8f6")
spec_dark <- c("Increased in periodontitis" = "#c2410c", "Decreased in periodontitis" = "#1c5cab")
ggplot(specificity, aes(perio_studies, other_conditions)) +
  geom_rect(data = distinct(specificity, direction), aes(xmin = 10, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = 15.5),
            fill = spec_light[as.character(distinct(specificity, direction)$direction)], inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  # one note per facet, naming its direction
  geom_text(data = distinct(specificity, direction) |>
              mutate(label = paste0("Commonly ", str_to_lower(str_remove(direction, " in periodontitis")),
                                    " in periodontitis,\ninfrequently in other conditions")),
            aes(x = Inf, y = -Inf, label = label, color = I(spec_dark[as.character(direction)])),
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = -0.5, size = 2.8, lineheight = 0.9) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = I(case_when(!spec_corner(specificity) ~ "grey70",
                                    direction == "Increased in periodontitis" ~ "#eb6834",
                                    .default = "#2a78d6"))),
             shape = 21, size = 2.6, color = "grey15", stroke = 0.4) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = taxon),
                  size = 2.6, fontface = "italic", color = "grey25", seed = 1, max.overlaps = Inf,
                  min.segment.length = 0.2, segment.color = "grey70") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~direction) +
  labs(x = "PerioSigDB studies reporting the genus in its periodontitis direction (log scale)",
       y = "Other BugSigDB conditions reporting the genus in the same direction") +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
```

The most-reported genera, *Porphyromonas*, *Prevotella* and *Fusobacterium*, are reported increased by dozens of other conditions. *Desulfobulbus*, *Fretibacterium*, *Filifactor* and *Tannerella* are commonly increased in PerioSigDB, but only 5–15 other conditions report them increased. Several of these are panel targets, which may raise their PerioSigDB counts.

## Whole-signature similarity to periodontitis

This comparison uses whole signatures, with taxa at their reported ranks (mostly species) rather than collapsed to genus. Each BugSigDB signature with at least 5 taxa is scored against the PerioSigDB consensus signatures (`r length(semsim$consensus$increased)` increased and `r length(semsim$consensus$decreased)` decreased taxa). The score is semantic similarity on the NCBI taxonomy, the best-match average of Lin similarity used by BugSigDB's tools. Smaller signatures give extreme scores, so they are left out. The first figure shows every condition with unadjusted p < 0.05 in any of its tests. The second keeps only the rows with FDR < 0.05 in at least one column, and the third shows each of those rows as one point.

```{r bsdb-semantic-c}

# conditions shown in the per-condition similarity figure: unadjusted p < 0.05 in any of their tests
sim_conditions <- unique(semsim_tests$stats$Condition[semsim_tests$stats$p < 0.05])
# body site rows left out of all similarity figures: colorectal cancer's mouth studies match the periodontitis
# consensus only in the opposite direction, so their direction may be flipped
excluded_site_rows <- tibble(Condition = "Colorectal cancer", site = "oral")

comparison_levels <- c("Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB increased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB decreased",
                       "Perio increased\nvs BugSigDB decreased", "Perio decreased\nvs BugSigDB increased")
label_comparison <- \(d) mutate(d, comparison = factor(sprintf("Perio %s\nvs BugSigDB %s", perio, direction),
                                                       levels = comparison_levels),
                                opposite = perio != direction)

# rows of the boxed figure: per condition, all of its units vs all other conditions first, then by p (same-
# direction columns) its units from each site group vs the same site group (where a proper background) and
# vs all of BugSigDB (only where p < 0.05 in some column and not the same units as the first row); without the
# excluded site rows
sim_rows <- function(res, conditions) {
  all_n <- filter(res$stats, kind == "all") |> select(Condition, direction, perio, all_n = studies)
  site_all_keep <- res$stats |>
    filter(kind == "site_all") |>
    left_join(all_n, by = c("Condition", "direction", "perio")) |>
    summarise(keep = any(p < 0.05) & !all(studies == all_n, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(Condition, site)) |>
    filter(keep)
  stats <- res$stats |>
    filter(Condition %in% conditions, kind != "site_all" | paste(Condition, site) %in% paste(site_all_keep$Condition, site_all_keep$site)) |>
    anti_join(excluded_site_rows, by = c("Condition", "site"))
  cond_order <- stats |> filter(direction == perio) |> summarise(p = min(p), .by = Condition) |> arrange(p) |> pull(Condition)
  gap <- 0.6
  rows <- stats |>
    summarise(p_same = suppressWarnings(min(p[direction == perio])), .by = c(Condition, kind, site)) |>
    mutate(Condition = factor(Condition, levels = cond_order)) |>
    arrange(Condition, kind != "all", p_same) |>
    mutate(pos = -(row_number() + (as.integer(Condition) - 1) * gap),
           label = case_when(kind == "all" ~ as.character(Condition),
                             kind == "site_all" ~ paste0("   ", site_names[site], " studies (vs all)"),
                             .default = paste0("   ", site_names[site], " studies (vs ", site_names[site], ")")),
           Condition = as.character(Condition))
  list(rows = rows, stats = stats)
}

# one box per condition and one row per set of study units (rows: Condition, kind, site, pos, label), with the
# rows named by bold in bold
similarity_boxes <- function(res, rows, stats, bold = rows$kind == "all") {
  keys <- c("Condition", "kind", "site")
  boxes <- rows |> summarise(ymin = min(pos) - 0.45, ymax = max(pos) + 0.45, .by = Condition)
  stats <- stats |> inner_join(select(rows, all_of(keys), pos), by = keys) |> label_comparison() |>
    mutate(significance = case_when(fdr < 0.05 ~ "FDR < 0.05", p < 0.05 ~ "p < 0.05", .default = "Not significant") |>
             factor(levels = c("FDR < 0.05", "p < 0.05", "Not significant")))
  units <- res$units |> inner_join(select(rows, all_of(keys), pos), by = keys) |> label_comparison() |>
    mutate(point_colour = factor(coalesce(site_names[site_group], "other"), levels = names(unit_site_colours)))
  shade <- distinct(stats, comparison, opposite) |> filter(opposite)

  ggplot(stats, aes(y = pos)) +
    geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = -Inf, xmax = Inf, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = "grey95") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, color = "grey50", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_rect(data = boxes, aes(xmin = -0.03, xmax = 1.03, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_quasirandom(data = units, aes(x = rank, color = point_colour), orientation = "y", width = 0.3,
                     size = 0.8, alpha = 0.6) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(xmin = mean_rank - ci, xmax = mean_rank + ci), width = 0, linewidth = 0.7,
                  color = "grey10", orientation = "y") +
    geom_point(aes(x = mean_rank, fill = significance), shape = 21, size = 3, color = "grey10", stroke = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = unit_site_colours, name = "Body site") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = "grey10", "p < 0.05" = "grey60", "Not significant" = "white"),
                      name = "Mean", drop = FALSE) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = rows$pos, labels = rows$label, expand = expansion(add = 0.3)) +
    # coordinate limits, not scale limits, so that bars reaching past 1 are clipped rather than dropped
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.03, 1.03), expand = FALSE, clip = "off") +
    facet_grid(. ~ comparison) +
    labs(x = "Similarity (share of other conditions' study units of the same direction it is more similar than; 0.5 = typical)",
         y = NULL) +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5), legend.position = "top",
          panel.spacing.x = unit(0.8, "lines"), panel.border = element_blank(), panel.grid = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_text(hjust = 0, face = ifelse(bold, "bold", "plain")))
}

sim_s4 <- sim_rows(semsim_tests, sim_conditions)

# rows of the main similarity figure (paper Figure 4B and C), chosen from the rows above. A row passes with
# FDR < 0.05 in any of its four columns. A body site group passes if either of its comparisons (vs all, vs the
# same site group) passes, and is shown by the one with the smaller p. A condition's passing site groups are
# shown where two or more pass, or where the whole condition does not pass; otherwise the whole condition is
# shown. Rows are ordered by their smallest p.
sim_main_rows <- function(stats, fdr_cut = 0.05) {
  pass <- stats |>
    filter(kind %in% c("all", "site_all", "site")) |>
    summarise(pass = any(fdr < fdr_cut, na.rm = TRUE), p = min(p, na.rm = TRUE), .by = c(Condition, kind, site)) |>
    filter(pass)
  whole <- filter(pass, kind == "all")
  sites <- filter(pass, kind != "all") |>
    slice_min(p, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(Condition, site)) |>
    filter(n() >= 2 | !Condition %in% whole$Condition, .by = Condition)
  bind_rows(filter(whole, !Condition %in% sites$Condition), sites) |>
    arrange(p) |>
    mutate(short = ifelse(kind == "all", abbrev(Condition), paste(abbrev(Condition), site_names[site]))) |>
    select(Condition, kind, site, short)
}
# row labels as in the paper figure: the condition on its first row, and for a body site group the site and
# what it is compared with, e.g. "COVID-19 (airway vs all)", "(gut vs gut)"
sim_main <- sim_main_rows(sim_s4$stats) |>
  mutate(first = Condition != lag(Condition, default = ""),
         pos = -(row_number() + (cumsum(first) - 1) * 0.6),
         site_text = paste0("(", site_names[site], " vs ", ifelse(kind == "site", site_names[site], "all"), ")"),
         label = case_when(kind == "all" ~ abbrev(Condition),
                           first ~ paste(abbrev(Condition), site_text),
                           .default = paste0("   ", site_text)))
```

```{r bsdb-semantic-boxes}
#| fig-width: 13.5
#| fig-height: !expr 1.4 + 0.36 * (nrow(sim_s4$rows) + 0.6 * n_distinct(sim_s4$rows$Condition))
#| fig-cap: "Similarity of BugSigDB signatures to the PerioSigDB consensus signatures, for all of a condition's study units and by body site group. Each study unit's mean best-match average Lin similarity is ranked against the study units of all other conditions with the same BugSigDB direction. The rank is the share of those units it is more similar than (0.5 = typical). Boxes: one condition each. First row (bold): all of the condition's study units, compared with all other conditions. Following rows, ordered by p: its study units from one body site group. These are compared either only with other conditions' units from the same site group (\"vs gut\", \"vs mouth\") or with all other conditions (\"vs all\"). Within-site rows need at least 20 such units from at least 10 other conditions in that direction, which excludes airway and eye. Rows against all other conditions appear only where p < 0.05 in some column and the condition has units from more than one site group. Colorectal cancer's mouth studies are left out: they match the periodontitis consensus signatures only in the opposite direction, so their direction may be flipped. Columns: similarity to the periodontitis-increased or -decreased consensus. White columns use BugSigDB signatures of the same direction, shaded columns the opposite direction. Conditions: those with unadjusted p < 0.05 in any row and column. They are ordered by their smallest p in the two same-direction columns, most significant at top. Small points: study units, coloured by body site group. Large point and bar: mean and 95% confidence interval. Black: FDR < 0.05; grey: unadjusted p < 0.05. Test: one-sided Wilcoxon rank-sum test of the units' similarities against those of the other conditions. Benjamini–Hochberg correction is applied within each column, separately for the three kinds of row. A row has no point in a column with fewer than 5 study units of that direction. Left of 0.5: less similar than typical. The test is one-sided, so this side is not tested."
similarity_boxes(semsim_tests, sim_s4$rows, sim_s4$stats)
```

Of these rows, `r nrow(sim_main)` from `r n_distinct(sim_main$Condition)` conditions reach FDR < 0.05 in at least one column. A body site group counts if either of its two comparisons does. A condition's body site rows replace it where two or more pass, or where the whole condition does not; otherwise the whole condition is kept. Colorectal cancer is the only condition that matches a periodontitis consensus in the same direction at FDR < 0.05 when compared with studies from its own body site. Its increased signatures resemble the periodontitis-increased consensus against all other conditions (FDR = 3e-06) and against other gut studies alone (FDR = 1e-08). Head and neck cancer's decreased signatures resemble the periodontitis-decreased consensus (FDR = 0.001), but much less so against other mouth studies (FDR = 0.2). Smoking and the mouth studies of rheumatoid arthritis resemble periodontitis only against all of BugSigDB, which is mostly gut. COVID-19 airway studies can only be compared with all of BugSigDB, because too few other conditions have airway studies. In the gut studies of COVID-19 and ulcerative colitis, the increased signatures resemble the periodontitis-decreased consensus when compared with other gut studies (FDR = 0.04 for both).

The next figure shows each of these rows as one point. The point shows in which direction the condition reports each periodontitis consensus: it compares how much its increased and its decreased signatures resemble that consensus. The axes match the direction summary above.

```{r bsdb-semantic-overview}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7.6
#| fig-cap: "In which direction each condition reports each periodontitis consensus: one point for each row of the figure above with FDR < 0.05 in at least one column, with body site rows chosen as described in the text. Similarity is the mean rank from that figure (0.5 = typical). Only similarity above 0.5 counts; a mean rank below 0.5 adds nothing. x: the periodontitis-increased consensus, the excess similarity of the condition's increased signatures minus that of its decreased signatures. Right means the condition reports these taxa increased; left, decreased. y: the periodontitis-decreased consensus, the condition's decreased minus its increased signatures. Up means the condition reports these taxa decreased; down, increased. Shaded: same direction as periodontitis for both consensus signatures. A direction with fewer than 5 study units is not tested and counts as 0. Point size: study units (both directions). Colour: the body site group of at least two thirds of the point's study units (grey: mixed). CRC: colorectal cancer; HNC: head and neck cancer; RA: rheumatoid arthritis; Smoking: smoking behavior; UC: ulcerative colitis."
# columns of the similarity figures, by BugSigDB direction . periodontitis consensus
ov_cols <- c("increased.increased" = "inc_same", "increased.decreased" = "inc_opp",
             "decreased.decreased" = "dec_same", "decreased.increased" = "dec_opp")
# excess similarity above typical (0.5); below typical counts as 0, and so does a missing comparison
excess <- \(r) pmax(coalesce(r, 0.5) - 0.5, 0)
ov <- sim_s4$stats |>
  inner_join(select(sim_main, Condition, kind, site, short), by = c("Condition", "kind", "site")) |>
  mutate(col = factor(ov_cols[paste(direction, perio, sep = ".")], levels = ov_cols)) |>
  select(kind, Condition, site, short, col, mean_rank, studies) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = c(mean_rank, studies), names_expand = TRUE) |>
  # x: the periodontitis-increased consensus, resembled by the condition's increased minus its decreased signatures;
  # y: the periodontitis-decreased consensus, resembled by its decreased minus its increased signatures
  # (organised by periodontitis consensus, like the axes of the direction summary)
  mutate(px = excess(mean_rank_inc_same) - excess(mean_rank_dec_opp),
         py = excess(mean_rank_dec_same) - excess(mean_rank_inc_opp),
         units = coalesce(studies_inc_same, 0L) + coalesce(studies_dec_same, 0L)) |>
  # colour: the body site group of at least two thirds of the set's study units (both directions), else mixed
  left_join(semsim_tests$units |> distinct(kind, Condition, site, unit, site_group) |>
              count(kind, Condition, site, site_group) |>
              mutate(share = n / sum(n), .by = c(kind, Condition, site)) |>
              slice_max(n, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE, by = c(kind, Condition, site)) |>
              transmute(kind, Condition, site,
                        main_site = ifelse(share >= 2/3, coalesce(site_names[site_group], "other"), ov_mixed)),
            by = c("kind", "Condition", "site")) |>
  mutate(main_site = factor(main_site, levels = names(ov_site_colours)))

# arrows on the 0 lines, pointing outward from the centre (as in the direction summary)
ov_lim <- 0.4
ov_h_arrows <- tibble(xend = c(ov_lim - 0.01, -ov_lim + 0.01))
ov_v_arrows <- tibble(yend = c(ov_lim - 0.01, -ov_lim + 0.01))

p_ov <- ggplot(ov, aes(px, py)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0, xmax = ov_lim, ymin = 0, ymax = ov_lim, fill = "grey94") +
  # dashed lines, with solid heads at the tips (a dashed arrow draws a broken head)
  geom_segment(data = ov_h_arrows, aes(x = 0, xend = xend, y = 0, yend = 0), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_v_arrows, aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = 0, yend = yend), inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "grey60") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_h_arrows, aes(x = xend - sign(xend) * 0.0005, xend = xend, y = 0, yend = 0),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  geom_segment(data = ov_v_arrows, aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = yend - sign(yend) * 0.0005, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE, color = "grey60", arrow = centre_arrow, linejoin = "mitre") +
  geom_point(aes(size = units, fill = main_site), shape = 21, color = "grey15", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_label_repel(aes(label = short, point.size = 8 * sqrt(units / max(units))), size = 3.2, color = "grey15",
                   fill = scales::alpha("white", 0.75), linewidth = 0, label.padding = unit(0.08, "lines"),
                   seed = 1, min.segment.length = 0, box.padding = 0.5, point.padding = 0.1, force = 4,
                   segment.color = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3, max.overlaps = Inf) +
  scale_size_area(max_size = 8, name = "Study units") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = ov_site_colours, name = "Main body site", drop = TRUE,
                    guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 4, alpha = 1))) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.4, 0.2),
                     sec.axis = direction_axes("Taxa decreased in condition\nresemble perio-increased taxa",
                                               "Taxa increased in condition\nresemble perio-increased taxa", c(-0.2, 0.2))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.4, 0.4, 0.2),
                     sec.axis = direction_axes("Taxa increased in condition\nresemble perio-decreased taxa",
                                               "Taxa decreased in condition\nresemble perio-decreased taxa", c(-0.2, 0.2))) +
  coord_equal(xlim = c(-ov_lim, ov_lim), ylim = c(-ov_lim, ov_lim), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Perio-increased consensus\n(increased minus decreased signature similarity)",
       y = "Perio-decreased consensus\n(decreased minus increased signature similarity)") +
  theme(legend.title = element_text(size = 9)) +
  direction_axis_theme
p_ov + theme(legend.justification = c(0, 1))
```

Head and neck cancer, smoking and the mouth studies of rheumatoid arthritis sit in the shaded quadrant: they report both consensus signatures in the periodontitis direction. Colorectal cancer matches only the periodontitis-increased consensus, so it sits to the right on the horizontal line. COVID-19 airway studies sit at the upper left: their decreased signatures resemble the periodontitis-decreased consensus and, more weakly, the periodontitis-increased one. The gut studies of COVID-19 and ulcerative colitis sit at the bottom, because their increased signatures resemble the periodontitis-decreased consensus.

## Colorectal cancer

### Species behind the shared genera

Colorectal cancer reports nine of the periodontitis-increased genera increased (direction summary above). Agreement at genus level does not mean the same organisms: a genus can be increased in both through different species. This figure compares the species each database names within those nine genera.

```{r crc-genus-species}
#| fig-width: 9.5
#| fig-height: 4.2
#| fig-cap: "The species reported within each genus increased in both periodontitis and colorectal cancer. Genera: the periodontitis-increased genera that colorectal cancer study units report increased, as in the direction summary. At least 3 units report each genus, and at least two thirds of them report it increased. Bars: the species named in increased reports within each genus, as shares of those reports. Left: PerioSigDB signatures; middle: BugSigDB colorectal cancer study units. The number of reports is at the right of each bar. Colour: the three species of the genus that periodontitis signatures report most, each with at least 10% of its reports and 2 signatures. They have the same colour in both bars; grey marks any other species. Right: how much the two species mixes overlap (sum over species of the smaller share; 100% = same mix, 0% = no species in common). Genera are ordered by overlap. Reports naming only the genus, or an unnamed species (sp., oral taxon, uncultured), are left out."
# the genera increased in periodontitis that colorectal cancer also reports increased (by at least two thirds
# of the >= 3 study units reporting them), as in the direction summary
crc_genera <- genus_agreement |>
  filter(Condition == "Colorectal cancer", perio == "increased", n >= 3, same / n >= 2/3) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  pull(taxon)
# entries named at genus or species rank within some genera; unnamed placeholders (sp., oral taxon, uncultured)
# are left out
named_entries <- \(names, genera) tibble(i = rep(seq_along(names), lengths(names)), name = unlist(names)) |>
  mutate(genus = ifelse(grepl("g__", name), sub("^.*g__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", name), NA),
         species = ifelse(grepl("[|]s__", name), gsub("_", " ", sub("^.*s__([^|]+).*$", "\\1", name)), NA)) |>
  filter(genus %in% genera, !grepl("[|]t__", name),
         is.na(species) | !grepl(" sp[.]| oral |uncultured|genomosp", species)) |>
  mutate(label = coalesce(species, "(genus level)"))
# PerioSigDB signatures and colorectal cancer study units naming each taxon, by direction
crc_units <- filter(bsdb_cc_sigs, Condition == "Colorectal cancer")
crc_species <- bind_rows(
  named_entries(dat$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`, crc_genera) |>
    transmute(source = "PerioSigDB signatures", id = i, direction = dat$`Abundance in Group 1`[i], genus, label),
  named_entries(bsdb_cc$`MetaPhlAn taxon names`[crc_units$sig], crc_genera) |>
    transmute(source = "Colorectal cancer study units (BugSigDB)", id = crc_units$unit[i],
              direction = crc_units$direction[i], genus, label)) |>
  distinct() |>
  count(source, genus, label, direction)
# species-level reports in the shared (increased) direction, as shares within each genus and source
crc_mix <- crc_species |>
  filter(direction == "increased", label != "(genus level)") |>
  mutate(source = ifelse(source == "PerioSigDB signatures", "perio", "crc")) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n), total = sum(n), .by = c(source, genus))
# overlap of the two species distributions: sum over species of the smaller share (1 = same mix, 0 = no species shared)
crc_overlap <- crc_mix |>
  select(genus, label, source, share) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = source, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) |>
  summarise(overlap = sum(pmin(perio, crc)), .by = genus)
# colour: periodontitis's three most reported species of each genus; every other species is grey
crc_top <- crc_mix |>
  filter(source == "perio") |>
  arrange(desc(n), label) |>
  mutate(top = row_number(), .by = genus) |>
  filter(top <= 3, share >= 0.1, n >= 2) |>
  select(genus, label, top)
genus_order <- crc_overlap |> arrange(overlap) |> pull(genus)
mix_plot <- crc_mix |>
  left_join(crc_top, by = c("genus", "label")) |>
  mutate(tone = ifelse(is.na(top), "other", paste0("top", top)),
         source = factor(source, levels = c("perio", "crc"),
                         labels = c("Periodontitis", "Colorectal Cancer")),
         genus = factor(genus, levels = genus_order),
         epithet = sub("^\\S+ ", "", label)) |>
  # segments: periodontitis's top species first, in order, then the rest by size
  arrange(genus, source, tone == "other", top, desc(n)) |>
  mutate(end = cumsum(share), start = end - share, .by = c(genus, source))
tones <- c(top1 = "#b5401a", top2 = "#e8703f", top3 = "#f4b08f", other = "grey72")
p_mix <- ggplot(mix_plot, aes(y = genus)) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = start, xmax = end, ymin = as.integer(genus) - 0.38, ymax = as.integer(genus) + 0.38,
                fill = tone), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  # species names inside segments wide enough to hold them
  geom_text(data = \(d) filter(d, share >= 0.16), aes(x = (start + end) / 2, label = epithet,
                                                      colour = tone %in% c("top1", "top2")),
            size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") +
  geom_text(data = \(d) distinct(d, genus, source, total), aes(x = 1.02, label = total),
            hjust = 0, size = 2.6, colour = "grey35") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = tones, breaks = c("top1", "top2", "top3", "other"),
                    labels = c("Periodontitis's main species", "2nd", "3rd", "Other species"),
                    name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "white", `FALSE` = "grey15"), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1), expand = expansion(add = c(0, 0.08))) +
  facet_wrap(~source) +
  labs(x = "Share of species-level reports (increased); right: number of reports", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"), panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "top",
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
p_overlap <- crc_overlap |>
  mutate(genus = factor(genus, levels = genus_order)) |>
  ggplot(aes(overlap, genus)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = overlap, yend = genus), colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(size = 2, colour = "grey20") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1)) +
  facet_wrap(~"Overlap") +
  labs(x = "Shared species mix", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))
fig_s3 <- p_mix + p_overlap + plot_layout(widths = c(4, 1))
fig_s3
```

Where colorectal cancer studies name a species, it is usually one of the species periodontitis studies report most often in that genus (coloured; `r sum(crc_mix$n[crc_mix$source == "crc" & crc_mix$label %in% crc_top$label])` of `r sum(crc_mix$n[crc_mix$source == "crc"])` named reports), led by *F. nucleatum*, *P. micra*, *P. stomatis* and *P. intermedia*. *Porphyromonas* agrees only at genus level: colorectal cancer studies name *P. asaccharolytica* and *P. uenonis* at least as often as *P. gingivalis*.

### Taxon-by-taxon similarity

This figure compares colorectal cancer's consensus signatures, built as for PerioSigDB, taxon by taxon with both PerioSigDB consensus signatures. Most cells show taxonomic relatives rather than exact matches.

```{r bsdb-crc-consensus}
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 10.5
#| fig-cap: "Lin similarity between the PerioSigDB consensus taxa (rows) and the colorectal cancer consensus taxa (columns). Higher means more closely related; 1 means the same taxon (outlined). Both consensus sets come from a binomial test of increased vs decreased reports, unadjusted p < 0.05. PerioSigDB counts signatures and colorectal cancer counts studies. Row colour: red, increased in periodontitis; blue, decreased. Brackets: PerioSigDB signatures (rows) or colorectal cancer studies (columns) reporting the taxon increased / decreased. The top-left and bottom-right blocks are the same direction as periodontitis. Rows are ordered by NCBI taxonomic lineage within each direction. Top strip: the column taxon's best-match similarity among the periodontitis-increased taxa, minus that among the periodontitis-decreased taxa. Red means more like increased and blue more like decreased, with full colour at a difference of 0.7 or more. Columns are grouped by family. Families are ordered by their mean difference, and taxa within a family by their own. The order runs red to blue for colorectal cancer's increased taxa and blue to red for its decreased taxa."

terminal_id <- function(x) paste0("NCBITaxon:", unique(sub("^.*[|]", "", x)))

perio_consensus <- tibble(
  id = unlist(semsim$consensus),
  perio_direction = rep(names(semsim$consensus), lengths(semsim$consensus))
) |>
  left_join(select(semsim$taxon_tests, id = ids, perio_up = increased, perio_down = decreased), by = "id") |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", taxon_sim$names[id], perio_up, perio_down))

crc_consensus <- bsdb_cc_sigs |>
  filter(Condition == "Colorectal cancer") |>
  mutate(taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig], terminal_id)) |>
  unnest(taxon) |>
  distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
  count(taxon, direction) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    n = increased + decreased,
    p = map2_dbl(increased, n, \(k, n) binom.test(k, n, p = 0.5)$p.value),
    direction = ifelse(increased > decreased, "increased", "decreased")
  ) |>
  filter(p < 0.05, taxon %in% rownames(taxon_sim$sim)) |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", sub(" <[^>]+>", "", taxon_sim$names[taxon]), increased, decreased))

# taxa reported by at least min_studies of a condition's studies, at least min_share of them in one direction
consistent_taxa <- function(cond, min_studies = 3, min_share = 0.75) {
  bsdb_cc_sigs |>
    filter(Condition == cond) |>
    mutate(taxon = map(bsdb_cc$`NCBI Taxonomy IDs`[sig], terminal_id)) |>
    unnest(taxon) |>
    distinct(Study, direction, taxon) |>
    count(taxon, direction) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = direction, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
    (\(x) mutate(x, increased = if ("increased" %in% names(x)) increased else 0L,
                  decreased = if ("decreased" %in% names(x)) decreased else 0L))() |>
    mutate(n = increased + decreased, direction = ifelse(increased > decreased, "increased", "decreased")) |>
    filter(n >= min_studies, pmax(increased, decreased) / n >= min_share, taxon %in% rownames(taxon_sim$sim)) |>
    mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", sub(" <[^>]+>", "", taxon_sim$names[taxon]), increased, decreased))
}

# heatmap of Lin similarity: PerioSigDB consensus taxa (rows) vs a condition's taxa (columns), with a
# strip showing the difference between each column taxon's best match among the periodontitis-
# increased and the periodontitis-decreased taxa (red: more like increased, blue: more like decreased,
# pale: like both or neither); within each block, columns are grouped by family (keeping relatives
# together), families ordered by their mean difference and taxa within a family by their own, red to
# blue for the condition's increased taxa and blue to red for its decreased taxa
taxon_family <- function(ids) {
  map_chr(strsplit(taxon_sim$lineage[ids], "|", fixed = TRUE), \(l) {
    fam <- grep("aceae$", l, value = TRUE)
    if (length(fam)) fam[1] else tail(l, 1)
  })
}
order_block <- function(ids, weights) {
  tibble(id = ids, w = weights, family = taxon_family(ids)) |>
    mutate(family_w = mean(w), .by = family) |>
    arrange(family_w, family, w) |>
    pull(id)
}
both_directions_heatmap <- function(cond, taxa) {
  shade <- \(x, col) rgb(colorRamp(c("#f7f3f1", col))(pmin(x, 1)), maxColorValue = 255)
  legend_sims <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1)
  taxa <- taxa |>
    left_join(select(taxon_sim$closest, taxon, sim_up, sim_down), by = "taxon") |>
    mutate(difference = sim_up - sim_down)
  up <- filter(taxa, direction == "increased")
  down <- filter(taxa, direction == "decreased")
  taxa <- taxa[match(c(order_block(up$taxon, -up$difference), order_block(down$taxon, down$difference)), taxa$taxon), ]
  row_levels <- c("Difference", rev(perio_consensus$label[order(perio_consensus$perio_direction != "increased",
                                                               taxon_sim$lineage[perio_consensus$id])]))
  cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(select(perio_consensus, id, perio_direction, row = label),
                              select(taxa, taxon, direction, col = label)) |>
    mutate(sim = taxon_sim$sim[cbind(taxon, id)],
           fill = ifelse(perio_direction == "increased", shade(sim, "#c0392b"), shade(sim, "#1c5cab")))
  strip <- taxa |>
    transmute(taxon, direction, col = label, perio_direction = "difference", row = "Difference", sim = NA,
              fill = ifelse(difference > 0, shade(pmax(difference, 0) / 0.7, "#c0392b"),
                            shade(pmax(-difference, 0) / 0.7, "#1c5cab")))
  bind_rows(cells, strip) |>
    mutate(
      row = factor(row, levels = rev(row_levels)),
      col = factor(col, levels = taxa$label),
      perio_direction = factor(c(difference = " ", increased = "Periodontitis increased",
                                 decreased = "Periodontitis decreased")[perio_direction],
                               levels = c(" ", "Periodontitis increased", "Periodontitis decreased")),
      direction = factor(paste(cond, direction), levels = paste(cond, c("increased", "decreased")))
    ) |>
    ggplot(aes(x = col, y = row, fill = fill)) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_tile(data = \(d) filter(d, !is.na(sim), sim > 0.999), color = "grey10", linewidth = 0.9, fill = NA) +
    # legend: the red scale (blue rows use the same scale); invisible tiles put every legend value in the data
    geom_tile(data = \(d) mutate(d[rep(1, length(legend_sims)), ], fill = shade(legend_sims, "#c0392b")), alpha = 0) +
    scale_fill_identity(guide = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1)), breaks = shade(legend_sims, "#c0392b"),
                        labels = legend_sims, name = "Lin similarity\n(blue rows:\nsame scale)") +
    facet_grid(perio_direction ~ direction, scales = "free", space = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(16)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 50, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
          axis.text.y = element_text(face = "italic"),
          panel.grid = element_blank(), strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
          legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(size = 9))
}

both_directions_heatmap("Colorectal cancer", crc_consensus)
```

Four taxa are shared exactly (*F. nucleatum*, *Peptostreptococcus*, *P. stomatis*, *P. micra*) and several more are close relatives. *Gemella*, increased in colorectal cancer, is closest to the periodontitis-decreased *G. haemolysans*. Colorectal cancer's decreased taxa, butyrate producers such as *Faecalibacterium*, have no close periodontitis counterpart.

### Do the periodontitis signatures rank high in colorectal cancer stool data?

Everything above compares published signatures. The BugSigDB paper also tested signatures directly on participant-level data (Geistlinger et al. 2024, Figure 3). It used ten colorectal cancer stool metagenome datasets from curatedMetagenomicData and ranked every BugSigDB signature by how strongly its genera differ between cancer and control samples. This analysis repeats that ranking with the periodontitis-associated genera added as two signatures, one per direction. Two colorectal cancer meta-analysis signatures (Wirbel et al. 2019 and Thomas et al. 2019) serve as positive controls. Those meta-analyses used several of the same datasets, so they should rank near the top.

Each point shows where one signature ranks in one dataset, as a top percentage: 1% means only 1 in 100 BugSigDB signatures is more strongly associated with cancer in that dataset. The tests ask whether a signature's genera differ between cancer and controls, not in which direction.

```{r crc-enrichment}
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "How highly the periodontitis signatures rank for association with colorectal cancer in each dataset. They are compared with about 1,600–2,100 BugSigDB signatures, those with at least 5 genera present in the dataset. Orange: the 19 periodontitis-increased genera. Blue: the 12 periodontitis-decreased genera. Grey: colorectal cancer meta-analysis signatures as positive controls (Wirbel 2019, square; Thomas 2019, triangle). Further right means a stronger association. Shaded: top 5%; dashed line: 50%, a typical signature. Filled: FDR < 0.05 across all signatures in that dataset and method. Rows: datasets with their cancer / control samples, largest at top. limma-trend tests each genus for differential abundance between cancer and control samples, on log counts per million. Over-representation analysis: hypergeometric test of the share of the signature's genera that differ at FDR < 0.05 (ties ranked last). PADOG: gene set test that down-weights genera shared by many signatures (1,000 sample-label permutations)."
# precomputed by scripts/crc_bugset_enrichment.R
crc_enrichment <- readRDS("../../output/crc_bugset_enrichment.rds")

# dataset names with spaces, as in paper Figure 5: "Yachida S 2019 (258/251)"
crc_datasets <- crc_enrichment$datasets |>
  mutate(label = sprintf("%s (%d/%d)", str_replace_all(dataset, "_", " "), n_crc, n_control)) |>
  arrange(n_crc + n_control)
crc_signature_colours <- c("Periodontitis increased" = "#eb6834", "Periodontitis decreased" = "#2a78d6",
                           "Wirbel 2019 meta-analysis" = "grey35", "Thomas 2019 meta-analysis" = "grey35")

fig_s6 <- crc_enrichment$ranks |>
  left_join(select(crc_datasets, dataset, ds = label), by = "dataset") |>
  mutate(ds = factor(ds, levels = crc_datasets$label),
         method = factor(toupper(method), levels = c("ORA", "PADOG"),
                         labels = c("Over-representation analysis", "PADOG")),
         signature = factor(label, levels = c("PerioSigDB_genera_increased", "PerioSigDB_genera_decreased",
                                              "Wirbel2019", "Thomas2019"),
                            labels = names(crc_signature_colours)),
         significant = fdr < 0.05) |>
  ggplot(aes(percentile, ds)) +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 0.1, xmax = 5, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "#fbe3d6") +
  annotate("text", x = 5, y = Inf, label = "top 5%", hjust = -0.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, color = "#c2410c") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50") +
  annotate("text", x = 50, y = Inf, label = "typical", hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, color = "grey40") +
  # lines between datasets, so each dataset's points are grouped together
  geom_hline(yintercept = seq_len(nrow(crc_datasets) - 1) + 0.5, color = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(aes(color = signature, shape = signature, fill = ifelse(significant, as.character(signature), NA)),
             size = 2.8, stroke = 0.9, position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +
  # reversed log scale: the more strongly associated signatures (smaller top %) on the right
  scale_x_continuous(transform = scales::transform_compose(scales::transform_log10(), scales::transform_reverse()),
                     breaks = c(0.1, 1, 10, 100), labels = c("0.1%", "1%", "10%", "100%")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = crc_signature_colours, name = NULL) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(21, 21, 22, 24), name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = crc_signature_colours, na.value = "white", guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~method) +
  labs(x = "Rank among BugSigDB signatures (top %, log scale)\nmore strongly associated with colorectal cancer →", y = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"), panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
fig_s6
```

The next figure shows the periodontitis-increased genera one by one in each dataset.

```{r crc-fold-change}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-cap: "The periodontitis-increased genera in each colorectal cancer stool dataset. Colour: log2 fold change of the genus between cancer and control samples (limma-trend), capped at ±4. Orange means more abundant in cancer, blue less abundant. White: genus not present in the dataset. Dot: FDR < 0.05. Genera are in the order of the direction heatmap; datasets as in the figure above."
fc_genera <- filter(perio_genera, direction == "increased")$taxon
fc_cells <- tidyr::expand_grid(genus = fc_genera, dataset = crc_datasets$dataset) |>
  left_join(filter(crc_enrichment$genera, signature == "PerioSigDB_genera_increased"), by = c("genus", "dataset")) |>
  mutate(genus = factor(genus, levels = fc_genera),
         ds = factor(crc_datasets$label[match(dataset, crc_datasets$dataset)], levels = crc_datasets$label),
         value = pmin(pmax(logFC, -4), 4))
ggplot(fc_cells, aes(genus, ds)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = value), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_tile(data = filter(fc_cells, is.na(value)), fill = "white", colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(data = filter(fc_cells, fdr < 0.05), size = 1.2, colour = "grey10") +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#1c5cab", mid = "#f0efec", high = "#c2410c", midpoint = 0, limits = c(-4, 4),
                       breaks = c(-4, -2, 0, 2, 4), labels = c("≤ −4", "−2", "0", "2", "≥ 4"), na.value = "white",
                       name = "log2 fold change,\ncancer vs control") +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 50, hjust = 1, face = "italic"),
        legend.position = "right")
```

The periodontitis-increased genera rank in the top 5% of BugSigDB signatures in 5 of 10 datasets with over-representation analysis and 7 with PADOG, and pass FDR in YachidaS_2019 and ZellerG_2014. Part of this ranking reflects genera they share with the meta-analysis controls (*Fusobacterium*, *Parvimonas*, *Peptostreptococcus*, *Porphyromonas*).
